title: Retime forwarding matches and WB data selection before their registers
motivation:
The champion scores 150.32 iterations/second at median Gowin Fmax
62.085 MHz and 4,130,235 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst vendor
path starts at MEM/WB rd, crosses forwarding and EX, and ends at a
fetch-predictor RAM address. A fresh unchanged-core placement-option-0
build reproduces 59.030 MHz and the exact 22.235 ns, 44-cell path.
A nearly tied path ends at dmem through the ordinary ALU. Both begin
with late producer-destination equality, then high-fanout operand
steering before execution. The accepted banked register file already
improved RF timing; replacing it with flops did not beat this champion.
Prior micro_opt training-feedback retiming left immediate recovery
and ALU paths limiting timing. Move the address comparisons earlier
without adding a pipeline stage or changing producer priority.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Apply one local forwarding-path retiming: move bypass address matching
and WB result selection to the input side of their existing pipeline
registers. Register four EX forwarding matches at ID/EX and the final
load-or-ALU WB value at MEM/WB. This is one bypass-network optimization:
both control and data are ready from registers before EX selects them.
Keep current two-bit forwarding selectors and EX operand muxes,
arithmetic, predictor, skid buffer and all instruction latencies.
No additional pipeline stage or prediction policy is introduced.

When ID accepts a fetch token, the current ID/EX producer advances
into EX/MEM and the current EX/MEM producer advances into MEM/WB.
Compare each incoming instr[19:15] and instr[24:20] against current
ID/EX.rd for next-cycle EX/MEM forwarding, and current EX/MEM.rd for
next-cycle MEM/WB forwarding. Include producer rd != 0 in each
comparison. Register these four Boolean results alongside ID/EX
using precisely its existing !stall payload enable. Reset them to
zero. They may be two independent two-bit output registers in
id_stage; core_pkg.sv and the existing packed payload need not change.

Replace forward_unit's live address equality/nonzero tests with these
registered matches. Continue to qualify the EX/MEM match with the
actual current EX/MEM ctrl.reg_write, and the MEM/WB match with the
actual current MEM/WB ctrl.reg_write. EX/MEM retains priority over
MEM/WB, and default remains saved ID/EX data. Qualifying with the
actual producer control, rather than guessed decode control, preserves
alignment-trapped jump/load write suppression and invalid bubbles.
Do not gate retained MEM/WB forwarding with retirement valid: its
data/control remain usable after valid clears during a dmem hold.

Retain the match bits on ID holds. On dmem backpressure, ID/EX and
EX/MEM hold and MEM/WB preserves its payload, so their relationships
remain exact. A load-use flush kills the held ID/EX controls/valid;
stale match bits cannot cause an architectural side effect. During
a blocking MUL/DIV, older forwarding slots can drain while ID/EX
holds. The ALU request and blocking_instruction_q already capture
the forwarded operands exactly once at ownership acquisition; retain
this behavior and do not reinterpret held match bits as fresh operands
after acquisition. The completion uses the captured metadata/result.
At the completion edge a newly accepted consumer compares against
the held M instruction's rd, correctly matching the producer entering
EX/MEM. Flush/recovery kills younger instruction controls as before,
and the next accepted token overwrites its match bits. Do not change
hazard equations, memory requests, forwarding data retention or the
captured blocking-operation lifecycle.

Also move the load/ALU writeback-data mux before the MEM/WB edge.
In mem_stage, capture in.ctrl.mem_to_reg ? load_data : in.alu_result
directly into the existing reg_q.alu_result slot, repurposed as the
unified registered WB result. In wb_stage, drive w_data directly from
this slot while retaining the existing w_en and w_addr equations.
Keep the existing read_data field/capture for compatibility, but it
no longer feeds the write-data mux. Preserve all other MEM/WB fields,
raw RVFI memory data/masks, trap controls and hold_wb behavior. Dmem
continues to use the unchanged EX/MEM effective address; selecting a
load's WB value must not replace its memory request or RVFI address.
Retaining the complete payload during hold_wb preserves exactly the
forwarding datum that the old separate ALU/load fields supplied.
Ordinary ALU, jump and M instructions have mem_to_reg=0 and capture
their original result unchanged. Loads capture the same sign/zero
extended load_data on the same edge as before. Actual reg_write still
suppresses trapped instructions; no new producer qualification arises.

This removes destination equality and zero detection from both the
forwarding-to-control-flow and forwarding-to-ALU clock intervals,
replacing them with four flop outputs and existing write qualification.
It also removes WB mem_to_reg selection from WB-to-EX and WB-to-RF
paths. The comparisons now run in parallel with ordinary decode/register-file
reads and terminate at the existing ID/EX edge. Predict unchanged
canonical stalled CoreMark cycles and an eight-percent fitness gain
from higher median Gowin Fmax. With unchanged cycles, acceptance
requires median Fmax above 64.94091 MHz and fitness above 157.23472.
Decode becoming critical, producer-control fanout and match/payload
misalignment under holds are the principal risks. Use the unchanged
vendor median and actual canonical marker cycles to evaluate the gain.

The complete prototype's Gowin placement options 0/1/2 reached

to dmem, versus the reproduced 22.235 ns forwarding/predictor path.
Options 1/2 are limited by registered WB data through EX to IF, with
worst arrival 20.174 ns. These results support removing both pieces
of bypass steering before execution, rather than moving the same
bottleneck between destination decoding and WB data selection.

title: Register complete bypass selections and unified writeback data
motivation:
The champion scores 150.32 iterations/second at 62.085 MHz with
4,130,235 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst Gowin path starts at a
MEM/WB destination-register bit, crosses forwarding and execute, and
ends in the fetch predictor. The prior structural flop-register-file
attempt exposed the same forwarding-to-ALU-to-dmem limit and reached
only 61.852 MHz. A complete operand stage previously failed stalled
random cosim, and registering IF/ID increased cycles without improving
timing. Retiming the bypass network at existing stage boundaries can
shorten both execution paths without adding any instruction latency.

passed eight trace-cosim runs and canonical CoreMark at unchanged cycles,
but measured only 61.981 MHz median. Its worst paths instead started at
producer write permission and the WB ALU/load-select bit. The proposed
structural change registers the complete bypass choice and its WB data
source, addressing those remaining serial decisions together.

boundaries. Generate the complete forwarding decision in decode for

near/far/saved selection for each source alongside its saved RF value.
In execute, select each operand with a parallel masked OR of the
EX/MEM result, the registered unified MEM/WB result and the saved RF
value. Execute must have no live destination comparison, write-enable
qualification or priority encoding before its operand muxes. This is
one restructuring of the bypass control and data pipeline; keep the
banked distributed-RAM RF, pipeline depth, fetch skid buffer, predictor
policy, blocking M units and nret=1 interface.

On a consumer capture edge, the near producer is the instruction
actually entering EX/MEM, normally the current ID/EX instruction. The
far producer is the instruction actually entering MEM/WB, normally the
current EX/MEM instruction. Match the offered instruction's raw rs1/rs2
fields against those destination numbers, excluding x0, and combine
each match with the producer's actual next-state write permission before
registering the choice. Derive near permission from execute's
trap-adjusted control and validity, and far permission from memory's
trap-adjusted control and validity. A misaligned JAL/JALR or memory
access must not claim a forwarding slot. Resolve newest-writer priority
before capture; when the near writer is canceled, choose a matching
permitted far writer or the saved RF value. Retain the existing load-use
interlock so an unready load address can never become operand data.
A current WB producer is already covered by write-first RF reads during
consumer capture; it is not one of these next-cycle forwarding sources.

Move WB's load-versus-ALU data selection to the input of MEM/WB. Capture
one unified write_value = mem_to_reg ? extended_load : alu_result
alongside the destination and write permission. Both WB-to-RF and
WB-to-EX then use this registered value directly. Preserve any existing
payload fields needed by RVFI or direct tests; synthesis may prune
redundant fields. The timed WB-to-EX path must not contain the old
mem_to_reg selection mux. During dmem holds retain the unified result,
destination and producer metadata while clearing only retirement
validity, as the existing MEM/WB forwarding contract requires. Avoid
qualifying retained forwarding data with WB.valid.

Keep forwarding selections aligned with the actual consumer token.
Hold them and its RF values on dmem or blocking-EX backpressure; kill
validity and side effects on load-use bubbles and recovery. ID/EX,
EX/MEM and the retained MEM/WB payload remain stable during dmem holds,
so a previously selected source stays usable despite WB.valid clearing.
When a load-use bubble clears, recompute the retained frontend consumer's
selection against the load now entering WB. When an M result completes,
use the saved blocking instruction's identity and write permission as
the near producer for the simultaneously captured consumer. Existing M
ownership must still capture fully forwarded sources once at request
acceptance and use that capture while older producers drain; live
selections during the owned wait must not recapture data. Derive matches
from actual next producers for exceptional transitions; do not assume
every stage advances together. Reset clears token validity and selection
state, and invalid tokens cannot advertise a producer or start effects.

A concrete implementation uses decode-side forward_unit inputs
id_rs1/id_rs2, near_rd = id_ex.rd, far_rd = ex_mem.rd,
near_write = id_ex.valid && ex.ctrl_with_trap.reg_write and
far_write = ex_mem.valid && mem.ctrl_with_trap.reg_write. For each
source choose 3'b001 on a permitted nonzero near match, otherwise
3'b010 on a permitted nonzero far match, otherwise 3'b100. Capture
these six bits inside id_stage's existing !stall payload update;
a flush/bubble can set them to the saved-value selection. The M owner
preserves its identity in ID/EX through completion, so these destination
inputs remain aligned in that implementation. Execute reads the captured
masks directly. Add write_value to mem_wb_t, assign it on ordinary MEM
advancement and leave it untouched by hold_wb. WB's w_data becomes a
direct read of write_value. Keep the rest of the proven pipeline intact.

There is no added pipeline stage, fast RAW bubble, live ALU-data bypass
into decode or extra arithmetic latency. Preserve decoder default-illegal
discipline, alignment traps, all RV32M and ALTOPS results, exact RVFI
source operands, channel-0 retirement order, memory-handshake stability
and once-only memory effects. All verification and fitness contracts
remain unchanged. Check in Gowin that the selection bits and unified
WB value are actual register boundaries and that EX paths start at
registered data or selections rather than unregistered tag comparison,
producer permission or WB result selection.

A temporary prototype of this complete topology was built in scratch
storage using the unchanged FPGA wrapper, stall generator and Gowin
evaluator. Placement options 0/1/2 reached 68.014/71.792/71.792 MHz,
giving 71.792 MHz median, 15.63 percent above the champion. Option 0
reports 3,518 logic cells, 1,015 registers, 32 RAM16s, 7 BSRAMs and
2 DSPs. Its worst path starts at the unified WB data register and
reaches dmem through operand selection and ALU, at 19.997 ns and
14 cells; the old destination-tag-to-forwarding path is removed.
All eight selftest/random1/random2/random3 trace-cosim cases passed,
including combined imem/dmem stalls. The unchanged run_coremark_ipc
evaluator validates canonical CRCs, UART, memory bounds and markers,
completing 10 iterations in exactly 4,130,235 bracketed cycles. Thus
prototype timing times IPC implies 173.82 iterations/second, about
15.6 percent above the 150.32 champion. These are prototype measurements,
not an accepted tournament result. In an isolated scratch copy of the
unchanged formal runner, wrapper, configuration and upstream framework,
52 of 53 checks passed; the reg_ch0 register-consistency proof remained
unfinished when the local 300-second experiment cap expired. This is
not a full formal pass: complete that proof and all normal unit/formal
gates during implementation without changing their settings or checks.
Predict 16 percent with medium
confidence. Preserve this topology rather than registering matches
alone, which did not improve fitness. Decode permission fanout, MEM
load extraction plus result selection, and remaining ALU/branch paths
are the main risks. Acceptance requires (new_Fmax / 62.085) divided
by (new_cycles / 4130235) to exceed 1.046; with unchanged cycles the
required median is 64.94 MHz.

title: Branch-discovered instruction streams in eight tagged replay blocks
motivation:
The champion's 64-entry BTB already removes most taken-transfer bubbles.
Prior one-loop replay saved 5.10 percent of CoreMark cycles but lost
enough Fmax to miss acceptance. Fresh prototypes on the current champion
show why replay should retain several loops without parallel wide range
lookups: one 128-word region still needs 3,919,730 cycles, while four
64-word regions reduce cycles further but substantially lower the clock.
Branch-discovered, directly indexed small replay blocks preserve streams
from several loops with simpler fetch lookup and fill controls.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one branch-discovered instruction stream predictor beside the existing
BTB and one-entry fall-through fetch skid buffer. Store eight directly
indexed, tagged, 64-byte replay blocks, each containing sixteen 32-bit
instruction words and sixteen fill-valid bits. Index blocks with fetch
PC[8:6], words with PC[5:2], and compare the selected full PC[31:9] tag.
A block is allocated only through discovery of a legal aligned taken
conditional backward branch whose PC-target span is at most 252 bytes.
Allocate every aligned 64-byte block intersecting that branch's target
through branch-PC interval. Already matching tags retain filled words;
a tag collision replaces that block and clears only its word validity.
No replacement pointer or parallel fetch-time interval comparisons are
needed. Retain allocated blocks across ordinary redirects and loop exits.

Register one copy of predictor_update_t for discovery only. Capture the
transaction every cycle, resetting/canceling its valid bit, and consume
each prior valid transaction once on the following edge, independently
of current fetch or EX holds. Derive the backward test, unsigned span and
block allocation entirely from this registered copy. Preserve original
immediate EX BTB training, forwarded branch resolution and recovery.

Implement eight constant-index generated blocks. Each owns an unreset
distributed_ram 16-by-32 payload array, a 16-bit fill bitmap, a 23-bit
full tag and one block-valid bit. The selected tag and fill bitmap feed
replay-hit; the selected payload word feeds replay data. For allocation
of slot r, form candidate page {candidate_tag, r[2:0]}. Choose candidate_tag
from discovery.target[31:9] when r >= discovery.target[8:6], otherwise
from discovery.pc[31:9]. Allocate only if this full page lies between
discovery.target[31:6] and discovery.pc[31:6], inclusive. The bounded
interval spans at most two adjacent 512-byte windows, so this selection
handles index wrap while preserving all upper address bits.

Capture real imemReady bus words whenever the current full PC matches
an allocated block, even when a full skid entry holds fetch at that PC.
Bus readiness denotes a valid response at the presented address; storing
that immutable word does not issue or retire an instruction. Gate a
block's payload write only with imemReady, selected full-tag hit and its
constant block index. Do not put fetch_accept, load-use backpressure,
live EX redirect, discovery replacement or FENCE.I on payload RAM write
enables. Validity determines ownership: reset/FENCE.I clear validity,
and replacement clears the selected word bitmap ahead of a simultaneous
old-tag fill, leaving any such payload write invalid for the new tag.
Replay-supplied tokens never fill payload or set a new word-valid bit.

Prefer current ready bus instruction data over replay. When imemReady
is low, a full-tag hit with the selected word filled supplies a valid
fetch token; otherwise retain the existing stall behavior. Set internal
availability to imemReady OR replay-hit and preserve existing skid
capacity, fall-through bypass, acceptance and ownership rules. Every
accepted token carries its exact PC, instruction and BTB-predicted next
PC. Immediate misprediction recovery still overrides bus and pipeline
stalls and kills all younger valid tokens. EX always validates actual
successors, operands and target alignment; replay does not predict
architectural effects or bypass any execution/hazard checks.

Add a FENCE.I flag to predictor_update_t immediately after valid. On a
legal advancing opcode 0x0f/funct3=1 instruction, invalidate every stream
block and fill bitmap, cancel pending discovery and force immediate
recovery to architectural PC+4, clearing the skid through normal recovery.
Reset and FENCE.I override discovery allocation and word-valid setting.
Keep the decoder's existing legality and architectural NOP result. Changed
instruction memory followed by FENCE.I must never retire stale replayed
or queued instructions. Preserve all existing pipeline/RVFI fields and
nret=1 ports, arithmetic, memory protocol and evaluation contracts.

A prototype of exactly this eight-by-sixteen topology was measured on
the current champion. All eight selftest/random1/random2/random3 full
trace comparisons passed, covering both zero-wait and combined bus stalls.
The unchanged run_coremark_ipc evaluator validated canonical CRCs, UART,
memory bounds, EBREAK and markers, reporting 3,745,064 bracketed cycles
versus 4,130,235 for the champion: 9.33 percent fewer cycles and 10.29
percent higher iterations/cycle. Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured
57.770/59.223/59.223 MHz, a 59.223 MHz median. Option 0 uses 5,002 logic
cells, 1,450 registers, 96 RAM16s, seven BSRAMs and two DSPs. The resulting
timing-times-IPC estimate is 158.136 iterations/second, 5.20 percent above
150.32, exceeding the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold. At these cycles,
acceptance requires median Fmax above 58.8854 MHz.

A directed IF-stage cocotb simulation also passed block-index wrap,
full upper-tag alias rejection, matching rediscovery, tag replacement,
FENCE.I overriding pending discovery/concurrent ready data, and reset
cancellation. These are prototype measurements, not an accepted result
or complete formal proof. Expect five percent fitness improvement with medium
confidence. The margin is narrow, so preserve the tested bank geometry,
full tags, bus-only fills and shallow write enables instead of expanding
capacity or adding training/recovery stages. Complete formal and full-core
changed-code FENCE.I checks during implementation, then run all unchanged
correctness gates and vendor median evaluation. Area/routing, tag alias
churn, and changed synthesis topology remain risks. No eval relaxation is
proposed; keep every legality, trap, RV32M, bounds, CRC and RVFI invariant.

title: Split and predecode EX result steering for arithmetic and memory addresses
motivation:
The champion's registered one-hot bypass choices raised median Gowin Fmax
to 74.535 MHz at 4,130,235 bracketed CoreMark cycles, but the remaining
worst path still starts at MEM/WB.write_value[17], crosses EX and the
general ALU, and ends at a data-memory BSRAM input: 19.124 ns and thirteen
cells. The memory interface currently takes its effective address from
the shared EX/MEM.alu_result bus, so arbitrary shift, compare, multiply
completion and ALU-result selection circuitry can constrain the physical
RAM address path even though loads/stores only require rs1 + immediate.
Prior register-file and complete bypass-mask improvements make that
unnecessary coupling the most promising remaining local micro_opt.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Specialize the existing EX/MEM memory-address datapath. Add a dedicated
32-bit effective_addr register field fed directly by the existing ALU
addition lane, before generic operation/result selection. For valid
LOAD/STORE instructions its operands are exactly the already forwarded
architectural rs1 and decoded immediate. Drive every MEM
address consumer from that field instead of the general alu_result:
io_dmemAddr, byte-lane masks, load extraction position, memory-alignment
checks, and the aligned RVFI memory address. Keep alu_result as the normal
ALU/branch-link/M result for writeback and EX/MEM forwarding. Loads continue
to select their extended memory data into MEM/WB.write_value, while stores
continue to use the original separately forwarded rs2 value.

Expose an internal add_result = a + b output from alu and use this same
named sum in the ordinary ALU_ADD result arm. Both consumers must share
the existing adder, retaining the existing ALU operand selection. The
address capture bypasses binary ALU operation/result selection, jump-link
override, and blocking M-result selection; do not duplicate the adder or
add another forwarding mux. Use full 32-bit modular rs1 + imm arithmetic, including all upper
bits and low alignment bits; do not truncate to the FPGA RAM address width,
pre-align requests, specialize to CoreMark addresses, or change the allowed
memory map. A valid legal LOAD/STORE has alu_src=1 and is_auipc=0, so this
value is bit-identical to its existing ALU_ADD effective address.

Clock effective_addr at the same EX/MEM boundary with the existing dmem
hold enable. Retain it while stall is asserted, so every pending LOAD/STORE
presents stable address, data and masks until acceptance. Give this field
its own next-state assignment after the normal EX/MEM bundle assignment:
on each nonreset, nonstalled edge capture alu_add_result, independently of
ex_wait, M ownership/completion, recovery, fast opcode or instruction
validity. Reset may clear it. The field is meaningful only for a valid
memory request; M operations and bubbles need no saved effective address.
This prevents the new address register from inheriting the general result's
wide bubble-clear or M-completion mux. Keep the existing EX/MEM controls,
validity and all other payload next-state priorities exactly intact.
No new pipeline stage, bypass source, issue rule or memory transaction is
introduced, and no load-use bubble is removed.

Use effective_addr consistently for both successful and misaligned memory
accesses. Preserve word/halfword alignment traps and suppress bus enables
and destination writes on those traps. RVFI still reports the word-aligned
address only for an actual nontrapped access, with the same original byte
masks, replicated store data and raw read word. A nonmemory instruction's
unused physical address can differ, but it must keep zero memory masks and
never create a read/write transaction. Preserve exact register results,
raw RVFI source operands, predictor feedback/recovery, once-only blocking
M requests and completions, stable held WB forwarding, nret=1 and contiguous
channel-0 retirement order. No multiplier/divider, ALTOPS, decoder legality,
FPGA wrapper, memory-map or correctness-contract change is proposed.

The prediction is unchanged canonical stalled CoreMark cycles and a
8-percent fitness gain from removing generic result steering from the
inferred RAM address timing cone. This is a local address-generation
micro-optimization with a specialized register path and the same shared
adder; no pipeline stage or instruction latency changes. At unchanged cycles, acceptance requires median Gowin Fmax above
77.96361 MHz and fitness above 188.76116 iterations/second. New register routing and a remaining redirect/ordinary-ALU path may limit
the gain. Run the unchanged correctness gates and measure actual canonical
marker cycles, CRCs and vendor median timing before claiming acceptance.

Complete this single EX result-steering specialization by predecoding the
ordinary writeback result before ID/EX. Add a twelve-bit fast_sel field:
bits 0..10 select ADD, SUB, AND, OR, XOR, SLT, SLTU, SLL, SRL, SRA, LUI;
bit 11 selects the JAL/JALR PC+4 link. Generate an exclusive mask from
validated decoder outputs in ID, capturing it under the existing !stall
payload enable. Illegal instructions and M operations select no fast lane.
Reset clears the mask; holds retain it. Flush kills existing validity and
side-effect controls without putting recovery on these mask payload flops.
No architectural effect may depend on an invalid mask.

In alu, select ordinary result lanes with parallel masked OR using those
registered bits, replacing binary fast-operation result steering. Reuse
add_result for its ADD lane, with the same expressions and signedness for
all other operations. In EX OR the bit-11-masked PC+4 link with this fast
result, avoiding a late is_jump result mux. Existing dedicated M completion
ports still supply exact MUL/DIV results to the original saved-instruction
completion path; preserve every real and ALTOPS formula and handshake.
Retain the existing operand forwarding and PC/immediate operand muxes.
The shared addition lane always feeds effective_addr regardless of the
fast-result mask, including on M/bubble cycles where no memory request is
valid. This specializes the two consumers of the same EX result network:
memory uses the unselected shared sum, while ordinary writeback uses a
predecoded selector. Do not add separate arithmetic units or pipeline stages.

title: Split execute effects into registered memory-address and recovery lanes
motivation:
The champion scores 180.46 iterations/second at 74.535 MHz and
4,130,235 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst Gowin path runs from
MEM/WB write_value through EX and the general ALU into the data-memory
address input: 19.124 ns across 13 cells. Registered bypass choices
have already removed producer matching and priority from EX, but
memory addresses still traverse general operand/result muxes, while
resolved next-PC feedback drives fetch and predictor memories directly.
Earlier structural fetch/operand-stage experiments either added cycles
without raising Fmax or failed stalled cosim. Replacing register storage
also left the same execution-to-memory limit. Preserve those lessons by
separating execute's externally applied effects at its existing output
boundary, rather than adding a general operand stage.

Scratch measurements against the unchanged wrappers show why this must
be one complete output-lane split. A dedicated address alone reached
only 71.281 MHz median and exposed forwarding-to-frontend feedback;
registered recovery alone reached only 69.288 MHz and retained the ALU
path into dmem. Separating and registering both effect lanes reached
80.738 MHz median, with the worst path now ending at an integer-result
register instead of either memory endpoint. This proposal selects that
single execution-output topology, not either incomplete prototype.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure execute's output into three parallel lanes at the existing
EX/MEM edge: the established integer writeback result, a dedicated
load/store effective address, and a registered frontend-recovery event.
Memory and frontend effects consume the latter two registered lanes;
they no longer consume the general ALU result or live EX decisions.
Fast arithmetic retains its existing latency and bypass structure.
There is no new ordinary execution stage, issue bubble or load-use
penalty. Recovery on a next-PC mismatch moves one cycle later and must
cancel the extra younger instruction now occupying EX. Keep nret=1,
the current retirement boundary, distributed-RAM RF, complete captured
forwarding selections, unified WB result, predictor policy, fetch skid
buffer and blocking MUL/DIV algorithms.

Add a full-width effective_address field to ex_mem_t. Compute it as
forwarded rs1 + registered imm, independently of alu_src, is_auipc,
ALU opcode/result selection and jump-link selection. Capture it beside
the existing integer alu_result on the same edge. In mem_stage use it
for dmem_addr, access alignment, byte mask position, load extraction
offset and aligned RVFI mem_addr. Keep all load/ALU write_value routing
and store-data forwarding unchanged. Preserve modulo-2^32 addition,
negative I/S immediates and complete MMIO addresses; never narrow to
the benchmark memory map. Populate the field in fast and saved blocking
metadata consistently. Existing EX/MEM holds retain the entire request,
and invalid/M tokens never acquire memory effects.

Keep branch conditions, alignment traps, resolved pc_next and the two
parallel predicted-successor comparisons in EX. Their valid advancing
mismatch produces a computed recovery event, but register redirect,
redirect_target and predictor_update_t before exposing them to IF.
Capture predictor feedback for each actual EX advancement exactly once;
nonadvancing cycles produce update.valid=0. Keep conditional training,
unconditional entries, target tagging and default non-control
invalidation behavior unchanged. Registered table feedback has one
cycle more latency. PC-relative and JALR arithmetic and the canonical
misalignment recovery successor remain exact.

An asserted pending registered recovery belongs to the older EX/MEM
instruction. Suppress younger EX advancement, predictor updates,
producer permission and all MUL/DIV requests while it is pending.
For the prototype, qualify is_mul/is_div, forward_write and advancing
with !redirect. On recovery, let the owning older instruction advance
through MEM/WB, squash the current younger EX token into an EX/MEM
bubble, and use the existing redirect inputs to flush ID/EX and the
fetch queue and set the fetch PC. No younger store may reach memory,
no younger M request may start, and no canceled instruction may train
or retire. Correctly predicted control transfers continue streaming.

Recovery must also work when a stale prediction belongs to a load or
store rather than a branch. Preserve EX/MEM on dmem stall BEFORE the
recovery bubble case, and retain the pending redirect bit until that
older request can advance. One concrete register rule is: reset clears
redirect; otherwise update it and redirect_target together only when !stall.
Hold the pending redirect_target as well as its valid bit throughout
any downstream stall; a held event must never change to the younger
instruction's computed target. Hold the older address/data/masks through every wait and accept its
memory effect exactly once. IF may receive the same pending recovery
while blocked, but must not consume younger tokens; the eventual
unblocked edge must annul the held ID/EX token. Never discard the
older memory instruction to apply recovery. Predictor update.valid is
a one-shot even while redirect is retained, so a prolonged memory stall
does not repeatedly train a counter. Pending payload needs no new reset
beyond validity/ownership cancellation. Preserve existing MEM/WB data
retention for forwarding during holds.

The concrete EX/MEM priority is reset, dmem hold, pending recovery
bubble, registered M completion, unfinished-M bubble, ordinary fast
token. Computed recovery requires in.valid && !redirect && !reset &&
!stall && !ex_wait. Capture the resolved target and complete predictor
update in registers; derive returned redirect only from its pending
register. The decoded M producer already retains its instruction and
forwarded operands through ownership. Since recovery suppresses the
extra younger EX token before request acceptance, no new M cancellation
protocol is needed. Preserve every existing RV32M and ALTOPS formula,
illegal/default decoder rule, alignment trap, RVFI operand and memory
field, contiguous channel-0 retirement and stable bus handshake.

A scratch prototype of exactly this topology, including older-memory
hold priority and retention of both the recovery bit and its target, used the unchanged vendor flow,
FPGA wrapper and timed stall generator. Gowin placement options 0/1/2
reached 71.743/80.738/80.738 MHz, giving 80.738 MHz median. Option 0
reports 3,533 logic cells, 1,182 registers, 32 RAM16s, 7 BSRAMs and
2 DSPs. Its worst path is 19.233 ns across 14 cells from the saved ID/EX rs1 value
to the EX/MEM integer-result register, rather than dmem or predictor
memory. All eight selftest/random1/random2/random3 trace-cosim cases
passed, including combined imem/dmem stalls. The unchanged
run_coremark_ipc validator passed canonical CRCs, UART, bounds and
markers: 10 iterations in 4,193,876 bracketed cycles, 1.54 percent more
than the champion. Timing times IPC predicts approximately 192.51
iterations/second, 6.68 percent above 180.46. These are scratch
measurements, not an accepted tournament result.

An isolated copy of the unchanged formal runner, wrapper, checks and
upstream framework has passed 52 of 53 checks on the preceding
prototype; register consistency remained unfinished at the local 360-second cap.
That prototype differs only in recovery/dmem-hold priority, which the
formal wrapper's tied-high ready signals cannot exercise. This is not
a full formal pass. Complete all ordinary gates on the final RTL and
add directed stale-prediction plus memory-backpressure coverage during
implementation without modifying any contract file or weakening tests.
The main risks are recovery age/hold mistakes, a slow register proof,
and placement variation. Acceptance requires (new_Fmax / 74.535) /
(new_cycles / 4130235) > 1.046; at the measured cycle count the median
must exceed 79.165 MHz. Predict 6 percent with medium confidence.

The C++ cosim harness has separate instruction and data memories, so
a self-modifying ELF cannot create the required stale-prediction
load/store corner there. Exercise that corner in cocotb by changing
the instruction delivered by the imem model after training a PC, while
retaining the predictor state. The existing eight trace cases passed
on the final scratch RTL; this additional directed corner is still a
required implementation test, not a claimed prototype pass.

title: Branch-discovered stream replay with registered operand bypass decisions
motivation:
The champion needs 4,130,235 bracketed CoreMark cycles and reaches
74.535 MHz with complete bypass priority registered in ID/EX. The
previous predictor experiment, hyp-20260930-003-r6s2, retained eight
tagged instruction blocks discovered by backward branches and reduced
cycles to 3,745,064, a 9.33 percent reduction. Its 59.591 MHz result
still had the previous forwarding topology: the worst path crossed
u_fwd and EX arithmetic. The champion has since removed those serial
forwarding decisions from EX. Applying the measured stream predictor
to this base is the most promising predictor opportunity: it attacks
the instruction-stall cost while preserving the newly improved clock
boundaries. The existing BTB already captures most direction/target
prediction benefit; another small direction predictor has less headroom.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one branch-discovered instruction stream replay predictor to the
champion's existing PC-only BTB and one-entry fall-through fetch skid.
Use eight directly indexed 64-byte blocks, each holding sixteen
instruction words, sixteen fill-valid bits, a full PC[31:9] tag and
block-valid bit. Select the block with PC[8:6] and its word with
PC[5:2]. Keep each 16x32 payload array unreset and explicitly marked
distributed_ram. Reset only ownership and validity. Preserve the
current ID/EX one-hot operand selections, trap-qualified producer
permissions, unified MEM/WB write_value and blocking MUL/DIV boundaries.

Capture EX predictor feedback in a register for stream discovery only.
Consume each registered transaction once, even while the pipeline is
held. A legal aligned taken conditional backward branch with unsigned
PC-target distance at most 252 bytes discovers the inclusive target
through branch-PC interval. Allocate all aligned 64-byte blocks that
intersect this interval. Matching block tags preserve filled words;
replacement installs the full tag and clears that block's word-valid
bitmap. For each constant block index r, select the target's PC[31:9]
tag when r >= target[8:6], otherwise the branch PC's tag, then require
the resulting full block address to lie inside the discovered interval.
This handles an interval crossing the 512-byte index wrap. Keep the
original immediate BTB training and EX misprediction recovery timing.

Fill instruction payload solely from real imemReady responses at the
presented PC when its allocated full block tag matches. A held full
skid may still fill the current word. Payload RAM write enables must
depend only on bus readiness, the fetch PC and selected block tag hit;
live EX redirect, fetch_accept, load-use backpressure and discovery
replacement must not feed these enables. Ownership changes govern
validity: a replacement or invalidation takes precedence over setting
a fill-valid bit, so a concurrent old-owner payload write cannot become
valid for the new tag. Replay data never fills another replay slot.

Prefer current ready bus data. When imemReady is low, a full tag hit
with the selected word filled supplies the instruction and internal
fetch availability. Use availability = imemReady OR replay_hit with
the existing skid acceptance, drain/refill and fall-through rules.
Each token carries the exact PC, instruction and BTB next-PC prediction
used when accepted. The fetch address remains the registered PC.
Ordinary redirects cancel younger queued tokens and override predicted
advancement; retained replay words remain protected by full tags and
fill-valid bits. Execution still validates every instruction's actual
successor, operands, legality and target alignment before retirement.

Add a fence_i feedback flag. A legal advancing opcode 0x0f/funct3=1
invalidates all replay ownership/fill validity, cancels pending stream
discovery and forces immediate recovery to architectural PC+4 so the
skid and younger instruction are discarded. Reset and FENCE.I take
precedence over allocation and fill validity. Preserve the decoder's
existing architectural FENCE.I NOP result. Changed code followed by
FENCE.I must be refetched before younger instructions retire. Keep
nret=1, all top-level IO, exact RVFI order and architectural fields,
trap discipline, memory side-effect checks and real/ALTOPS arithmetic.

At the previous replay cycle count, unchanged champion Fmax would yield
approximately 199.03 iterations/second, a 10.29 percent fitness gain.
Acceptance above 180.46 x 1.046 requires median Fmax above approximately
70.69 MHz at those cycles. Expect an eight percent gain, with medium
confidence: distributed replay storage increases area/routing and may
change Gowin register absorption or placement. Validate actual marker
cycles, canonical CRCs and vendor median Fmax on this champion rather
than assuming the prior cycle count and clock gain compose exactly.

title: Capture complete ALU operand choices before ID/EX
motivation:
The champion reaches 192.51 iterations/second at 80.738 MHz median
Gowin Fmax and 4,193,876 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its placement-0
critical path starts at saved ID/EX.rs1_val[11] and ends at
EX/MEM.alu_result[29], with 19.233 ns arrival and fourteen cells.
A fresh unchanged vendor build reproduces that report. It traverses
two raw forwarding LUTs and then an AUIPC-versus-rs1 operand LUT before
the ALU. The second path starts at a forwarding selection, traverses
the analogous register-versus-immediate operand network, and reaches
alu_result[0] at 19.210 ns. The accepted complete bypass masks removed
writer comparisons and priority from EX, but the later PC/immediate
choices remain serial with data forwarding. LESSONS.md and the
micro_opt history establish that register-file banking and complete
one-hot bypass selections are valuable, while match-only retiming and
r7s0 result/address predecode did not improve the champion. Extend the
successful selection principle to these remaining operand muxes.

Gowin Fmax and 4,193,876 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its placement-0
critical path starts at saved ID/EX.rs1_val[11] and ends at
EX/MEM.alu_result[29], with 19.233 ns arrival and fourteen cells.
A fresh unchanged vendor build reproduces that report. It traverses

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Apply one local micro-optimization: fuse forwarding and ALU operand-source
selection into complete four-way one-hot choices captured at the
existing ID/EX boundary. EX then masks registered candidate data once
instead of selecting a forwarded register and subsequently selecting
PC or immediate. Preserve the established five-stage pipeline, ordinary
instruction latency, load-use interlock, blocking M algorithms,
registered recovery, independent effective-address lane, predictor,
fetch skid buffer, retirement boundary and nret=1 port contract.

Add two four-bit payload fields, alu_a_sel and alu_b_sel, to id_ex_t.
Bits 0, 1 and 2 select the next EX/MEM result, next MEM/WB unified value
and saved write-first RF value respectively. Bit 3 selects the saved
instruction PC for operand A, and the decoded immediate for operand B.
In ID form alu_a_sel = dec_is_auipc ? 4'b1000 : {1'b0,fwd_rs1_sel}
and alu_b_sel = dec_alu_src ? 4'b1000 : {1'b0,fwd_rs2_sel}. Capture both
under the existing !stall payload enable, using the offered instruction's
validated decoder outputs and the already complete forwarding priority.
Reset clears them with the existing bundle reset. Holds retain them.
Existing flush/bubble validity and side-effect cancellation remains in
force; a killed token's unused selector payload may retain its value.
A valid accepted token always carries exactly one selected source for
each ALU operand.

Replace the two late alu_a/alu_b conditional muxes in EX with parallel
four-term masked ORs of the selected registered data. For A the candidates
are fwd_ex_mem, fwd_mem_wb, in.rs1_val and in.pc; for B they are
fwd_ex_mem, fwd_mem_wb, in.rs2_val and in.imm. Do not feed these ALU
operands through the old raw rs1/rs2 muxes first. Preserve the existing
three-bit raw forwarding masks and raw rs1/rs2 network for architectural
RVFI source values, store data, branch conditions, JALR and the independent
rs1 + immediate memory address. AUIPC must still report its architectural
raw source fields independently of its PC arithmetic input, and immediate
instructions must retain the original raw rs2 metadata. Leave binary ALU
operation/result selection and EX/MEM result/metadata priority unchanged.

The selector choices must follow the actual token across dmem holds,
load-use bubbles, recovery and blocking M ownership. A load-use consumer
recomputes its choice when it finally captures; it never forwards a load
address as data. An M request captures the newly selected forwarded ALU
operands once, and uses those captured operands throughout execution even
as older forwarding producers drain. At completion the held ID/EX identity
still advertises the existing near producer for the next consumer.
MEM/WB retains its unified data during stalls despite retirement-valid
clearing. Preserve newest-writer priority, x0, write-first RF behavior,
misalignment write cancellation, exact real RV32M and ALTOPS results,
full-width modular arithmetic, recovery age and stable pending memory
requests. Invalid selectors cannot start M operations or create any write,
memory transaction, predictor update or retirement. All legality, memory,
RVFI and fitness checks remain mandatory.

A temporary prototype implements exactly these two new fields, their ID
capture and the two EX masked-OR operands; every other champion RTL module
is unchanged. With the unchanged FPGA wrapper and timed stall generator,
Gowin placements 0/1/2 reach 87.658/87.839/87.839 MHz, giving 87.839 MHz

title: Separate execute result capture from pipeline token ownership
motivation:
The champion scores 192.51 iterations/second at 80.738 MHz and
4,193,876 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst reported Gowin path
starts at ID/EX.rs1_val and ends at EX/MEM.alu_result through the ALU,
taking 19.233 ns across fourteen cells. Registered bypass choices and
independent memory-address/recovery lanes have removed earlier limits.
Integer results still traverse the general ALU's M-result selection
and the EX/MEM bundle's reset, hold, recovery, M-completion and bubble
priorities. Several of those decisions are needed to own a token,
but do not need to select or clear its thirty-two result bits.
Structural history shows that adding an operand stage can break
stalled execution, while registering complete decisions at existing
boundaries can improve timing without changing CoreMark cycles.

integer-result payload and the established instruction-ownership/control
token. Keep one shared full-width EX/MEM result register, but give it a

parallel lanes: ordinary integer/link results, the registered multiply

retirement metadata. This is one structural repartition of result
capture and ownership, with no added stage, instruction latency, RAW

Expose an internal fast_out from alu containing exactly the ordinary
ADD/SUB, logic, compare, shift and LUI results; its M/default arms are
zero. Keep the original out behavior for direct ALU users and tests by
selecting the existing dedicated mul_result/div_result ports for M
operations and fast_out for ordinary operations. Execute consumes
fast_out rather than the all-operation out, so its ordinary path has
no redundant selection of M results inside the ALU. JAL/JALR retain
their existing PC+4 override in the ordinary lane. Leave every real
RV32M algorithm, correction step, ALTOPS formula and handshake intact.

Define D = div_owned_q && div_result_valid and
M = mul_owned_q && mul_result_valid, using the existing mutually
exclusive ownership state. On each nonreset, nonstalled edge capture
result_payload = ({32{!D && !M}} & fast_instruction.alu_result) |

validity, request acceptance, or the priority that clears the token
bundle. In particular, recovery and unfinished-M cycles may capture
irrelevant payload while their token remains invalid and side-effect
free. Preserve reset-to-zero and retain the result register whenever
dmem stalls. A completed M operation selects its stable registered
result on the same edge that its saved instruction enters EX/MEM.

A concrete implementation can retain reg_q.alu_result as the separate
payload register: after the existing bundle next-state assignments,
override that field with the flat expression above under !reset &&
!stall. This overrides irrelevant result clears and copies while every
other field keeps its established transition. Present out.alu_result

title: Registered fetch tokens break the instruction-stream replay feedback path
motivation:
The champion scores 192.51 at 80.738 MHz over 4,193,876 marker-bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its 64-entry next-PC predictor already captures most
branch-direction benefit. The prior eight-block stream predictor saved
9.33 percent of cycles on the preceding champion but reached only
64.584 MHz. Its worst path ran from replay ownership through IF and the
hazard unit back into a replay word-index register. Repeating that
fall-through replay frontend would recreate the demonstrated bottleneck.
Registering fetched instruction tokens can separate replay availability
and data selection from decode hazards while retaining the measured
instruction-stall savings. This is one stream-predictor hypothesis;
changes to frontend buffering serve that predictor's timing boundary.

A scratch prototype on the exact current champion uses 3,868,725
bracketed cycles with both standard pseudo-random bus stalls, a 7.75
percent reduction. The canonical five CRCs, validation literal,
EBREAK completion and OOB check all pass. Unchanged selftest and three
random-program RVFI cosim comparisons also pass with both bus stalls.
On the corrected scalar-token RTL, vendor placement options 0/1/2
report 80.111/82.513/82.513 MHz, giving a median of 82.513 MHz and
approximately 213.28 iterations/second, 10.79 percent above 192.51.
Area is 5,143 LUT4 and 1,684 FF, with 96 LUTRAM, seven BSRAM and two
DSP. This is prototype evidence, not an accepted tournament result.
The unchanged isolated formal suite passed 52 of 53 checks; register
consistency remained unfinished at the local 420-second cap, with no
reported assertion failure. This is not a full formal pass. Complete
that check and all ordinary implementation gates without changing
wrappers, depths, assumptions, or any other correctness contract.
Scratch cocotb checks also pass replay during bus stalls, full upper
tags, ready-bus precedence, replacement concurrent with old-owner
fill, FENCE.I priority over pending discovery/fill, and 2,000 cycles
of randomized FIFO holds, drain/refill, recovery and reset.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add branch-discovered instruction stream replay behind a registered
two-token fetch FIFO, replacing the current fall-through skid path.
ID must consume only a previously registered complete token. Never
expose a live bus/replay instruction or live replay-hit bit to decode,
forwarding comparisons, or the load-use hazard unit, even when empty.
An empty FIFO therefore inserts one initial/refill latency cycle, but
simultaneous enqueue/dequeue maintains one instruction per cycle in
a warm stream. Determine FIFO dequeue from its registered head valid
and the existing ID backpressure; determine fetch capacity from FIFO
occupancy and that dequeue. Raw source availability gates enqueue
and predicted-PC advancement only. It must not feed ID readiness or
feed back through hazard logic into replay RAM address enables.

Represent the FIFO payload as two separately named if_id_t registers,
a registered head/tail pointer and a two-bit occupancy count. Select
the head with an explicit mux and write each slot with its constant
slot select. Avoid an unpacked array of typedef-struct tokens: the
scratch Yosys frontend interpreted its dynamic access as a bit select,
eliminating instruction payload and making retirement unreachable.
This must be fixed in RTL, never by bypassing formal checks.

Retain the existing PC-only tagged BTB, EX/MEM-owned registered recovery,
ID/EX one-hot bypass selections, registered effective addresses, unified
writeback, and blocking multiplication/division. At enqueue capture PC,
instruction and the exact pre-edge predicted_next_pc together. Enqueue
at most once per PC advance; hold the presented imem address when no
fetch is accepted. Allow full FIFO drain/refill without overwriting its
old head. Recovery clears all queued younger tokens, overrides source
readiness and FIFO capacity, and retains its existing older-owner
priority during dmem stalls. A recovery edge cannot enqueue a token.

Retain eight directly indexed 64-byte replay blocks discovered by legal,
aligned, taken conditional backward branches spanning at most 252 bytes.
Index blocks with PC[8:6], words with PC[5:2], and compare full PC[31:9]
tags. Each block owns sixteen unreset 32-bit distributed-RAM words and
a separate ownership bit and sixteen fill-valid bits. Registered EX
feedback allocates every block intersecting the inclusive target-to-PC
interval, including index wrap; matching ownership preserves words,
replacement clears fill validity. Avoid parallel whole-interval fetch
comparisons. Fill only real imemReady words at the currently presented
PC with matching ownership, independently of enqueue, ID hazards and
ordinary recovery. Replacement/invalidation wins over fill validity,
so a simultaneous old-owner write cannot validate a new-owner word.
Prefer current ready bus data; otherwise a tagged filled replay word
supplies the FIFO input. Never fill replay from replay-supplied data.

Replay source validity/data end at the fetch-token register boundary.
Use asynchronous RAM16 reads addressed by the registered fetch PC and
shallow constant-bank write controls. Do not introduce per-bank word
address registers enabled by the fall-through hazard expression from
the failed replay implementation. Keep FIFO payload updates separate
from reset/redirect validity handling so recovery does not gate wide
data enables or replay payload writes.

Add one fence_i flag to registered predictor feedback. A legal advancing
FENCE.I invalidates replay ownership/fill state, cancels pending discovery,
and forces the existing registered recovery to architectural PC+4,
flushing queued and younger decoded instructions. Reset and FENCE.I
win over discovery and validity fills. Preserve current decoder legality,
alignment traps, exact RVFI order and nret=1 IO; execution still validates
every captured prediction against the architectural next PC.

The added registered IF boundary costs a cycle after recovery, and the
prototype's measured cycle count already includes that cost. At
3,868,725 cycles, acceptance above 192.51 x 1.046 requires median Fmax
above 77.903 MHz; the measured 82.513 MHz median clears it. Expect a
ten percent fitness gain with medium confidence. The decisive risks
are correctness in replay ownership/FENCE.I corners and implementation
drift that restores wide recovery enables or a live fetch-to-ID path.
Verify the unmodified formal/cosim gates, canonical stalled CoreMark CRCs,
actual marker cycles and median vendor timing; simulation alone cannot
establish the gain. Change only the listed RTL and cocotb tests.

title: Three-stage radix-4 barrel shifting with shared arithmetic fill
motivation:
The champion scores 209.45 at 87.839 MHz and 4,193,876 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its worst Gowin path runs from EX/MEM.alu_result[27]
to EX/MEM.alu_result[7] through the ALU in 16.702 ns across twelve
cells. Accepted operand preselection has removed serial forwarding
decisions, leaving ordinary ALU implementation as a timing opportunity.
Existing SLL/SRL/SRA use separate dynamic shift expressions. Prior
micro_opt history supports shortening combinational paths at unchanged
instruction cycles; the sibling result-ownership partition did not
beat the current champion. A local grouped shifter is a distinct angle.

The champion scores 209.45 at 87.839 MHz and 4,193,876 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its worst Gowin path runs from EX/MEM.alu_result[27]
to EX/MEM.alu_result[7] through the ALU in 16.702 ns across twelve
cells. Accepted operand preselection has removed serial forwarding

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only ordinary shift implementation in alu.sv with explicit
radix-4 grouped barrel networks. Keep the binary operation encoding,
existing ALU ports, complete registered operand selections, pipeline
boundaries and instruction latencies unchanged. There is no additional
register, stall, prediction policy or execution stage.

Build separate left and right data networks, each with three steps.
Decode b[1:0] into low_sel = 4'b0001 << b[1:0] and b[3:2] into
mid_sel = 4'b0001 << b[3:2]. The first step selects shifts of 0/1/2/3
bits; the second selects 0/4/8/12 bits; the final step selects 0/16
bits using b[4]. Express each four-way step as an OR of four data
terms masked by the mutually exclusive selector bits. Use fixed slices
and concatenations rather than variable shift expressions inside the
network. Left shifts always fill zero. Both SRL and SRA share the
right network, with fill = (op == ALU_SRA) && a[31]; each fixed right
shift concatenates the required number of copies of this original fill
bit. Right fill remains correct through both grouped steps and the

title: Bank-local next-PC decisions preserve the instruction replay clock
motivation:
The champion scores 209.45 iterations/second at 87.839 MHz over
4,193,876 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its existing 64-entry
next-PC predictor already captures most branch-direction benefit:
earlier architectural modeling found only 4,384 fewer errors when
increasing the table to 128 entries. Instruction stream replay has
substantially more measured headroom under the contracted bus stalls.

The last predictor attempt, hyp-20260930-003-r8s2, passed formal and
cosim and reduced the marker interval to 3,868,195 cycles by combining
eight branch-discovered replay blocks with a registered two-token
frontend. Its 78.941 MHz median made fitness only 204.08. The reported
worst path was fetch PC to the BTB tag memory, with 31 logic cells;
the earlier fall-through replay attempt instead exposed a replay-hit
through hazard backpressure to replay address-register path. These
results identify a frontend implementation bottleneck rather than
insufficient replay coverage. Explicit RAM16 banking has already
improved the register file on this FPGA. Apply that storage discipline
to predictor lookup while retaining a registered replay-to-ID boundary.

A scratch prototype on the exact champion confirms why banking alone
is insufficient: selecting a bank's full tag before comparing it gave
only 80.412 MHz median. Comparing tag, validity and direction locally
within each bank, then combining masked target words, gave vendor
placement-option Fmax values of 78.893/87.662/87.662 MHz. Its median is
87.662 MHz and its standard stalled CoreMark interval is 3,868,725
cycles, yielding 226.59 iterations/second, 8.18 percent above 209.45.
All five canonical CRCs, the validation literal, EBREAK completion
and the OOB check pass. Selftest and all three random-program RVFI
cosim comparisons also pass with both bus stalls. Area is 6,075 LUT4,
1,782 FF, 176 LUTRAM, four BSRAM and two DSP. Full formal has not been
run on this scratch variant; historical r8s2 passing formal does not
establish a formal pass for this proposal. Complete every normal gate.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one instruction stream predictor: retain previously fetched
words in eight tagged 64-byte blocks discovered by resolved backward
branches, and replay them when the instruction bus is unavailable.
Use the proven registered two-token fetch topology from r8s2, but
explicitly bank the associated 64-entry next-PC table into four
independent 16-entry asynchronous-read distributed-RAM banks with
bank-local prediction decisions. The local decisions are essential:
banking followed by a wide tag mux missed the acceptance clock in
the scratch experiment. Keep the established prediction algorithm
and table capacity.

Split BTB tags and targets by PC[7:6], with PC[5:2] addressing each
RAM16 bank. Retain full PC[31:8] tags, target[31:2], unconditional
bits, valid bits and saturating two-bit counters. Declare payload
memories inside constant-index generate banks with distributed_ram
attributes, asynchronous reads and bank-local synchronous writes.
Reset only validity. In each constant bank independently compare its
asynchronous tag read against fetch PC[31:8] and combine equality,
entry validity, PC[7:6] matching that bank, and unconditional/counter
direction to produce a one-bit predict_bank signal. Mask that bank's
30-bit target with predict_bank and OR all four targets; select this
result versus PC+4 with the OR of predict_bank. Do not select a wide
tag or wide counter/target tuple before performing the tag comparison.
The implementation must preserve the locally resolved decision before
target selection, rather than merely adding distributed_ram hints.
Preserve a pre-edge lookup on concurrent training, including identical-index
lookup/update. Give update-hit detection its own asynchronous tag and
counter read view if inference requires replication; do not serialize
training through the prediction read or add a live training bypass.
Check the vendor synthesis report actually maps these payload arrays
to RAM16 rather than BSRAM. Do not introduce a pipeline cycle into
the next-PC recurrence or attach decode/hazard-dependent enables to
predictor read addresses. PC-only prediction must not depend on
instruction data, replay hit, or EX operands.

ID receives only complete previously registered if_id_t tokens from
two separately named scalar payload registers and two-bit occupancy.
Use a fixed head and tail: dequeue from a two-token queue copies tail
to head; enqueue writes the slot left empty after the simultaneous
dequeue. With one queued token and simultaneous dequeue/enqueue, the
new token replaces head directly. These are explicit scalar writes,
without a dynamic struct-array index or extra head/tail pointers.
An unpacked struct array with dynamic access is
unsuitable for the existing Yosys frontend. Capture PC, instruction
and the exact predicted_next_pc together. An empty queue has one
refill cycle, while simultaneous dequeue/enqueue sustains one token
per cycle. Head availability comes only from registered occupancy;
decode backpressure determines dequeue and available capacity. Raw
bus/replay availability determines enqueue and PC advancement only,
and must never become the hazard unit's instruction-availability
input. Keep wide payload enables independent of redirect; validity
and occupancy cancel every younger token on recovery. Recovery wins
over source readiness and queue fullness and cannot enqueue a token.

Each replay block is directly indexed by fetch PC[8:6], compares
PC[31:9], and owns sixteen unreset 32-bit distributed-RAM words with
sixteen fill-valid bits. Use PC[5:2] as the asynchronous word address,
without address-register enables driven by decode hazards. Registered
once-per-advance EX feedback discovers legal aligned taken conditional
backward branches whose inclusive target-to-branch interval spans at
most 252 bytes. Register per-bank discovery mask and new tags before
applying descriptor changes; discovery has no decode-dependent enable.
Allocate every intersecting block, including index
wrap; preserve matching ownership and invalidate all words on tag
replacement. Descriptor writes and word fills use constant-bank local
controls. Avoid parallel full-region comparisons in the fetch path.

Fill only real ready-bus words at the currently presented imem PC with
matching replay ownership. Filling is independent of FIFO capacity,
decode holds, and ordinary recovery, since these are immutable bus
observations. Never fill from replay data. Prefer current ready-bus
data; otherwise a matching filled replay word supplies enqueue even
when io_imemReady is zero. Replacement and invalidation take priority
over fill validity: an old-owner write concurrent with replacement
cannot mark a new-owner word valid. Full PC tags remain architectural;
do not hardcode CoreMark addresses or shorten tags to its working set.

A legal advancing FENCE.I produces registered invalidation feedback
and sequential recovery to architectural PC+4. It clears all replay
ownership/fill validity and cancels pending discovery, ahead of every
allocation/fill, and flushes queued or decoded younger instructions.
Reset has the same validity priority. Retain EX/MEM-owned recovery
and its target across older dmem holds, one-shot predictor training,
existing squash of younger stores and arithmetic requests, exact
captured predictions through stalls, and resolution of every valid
instruction against its architectural successor. Keep the champion's
complete ALU operand choices, blocking M arithmetic, decoder default
legality, alignment traps, bus protocol and nret=1 RVFI contract.

The prototype's cycle count includes registered-queue refill and
recovery latency. At 3,868,725 cycles, exceeding the champion by the
required 4.6 percent needs median Fmax above 84.758 MHz. Its measured
87.662 MHz clears that threshold, supporting an eight percent expected
fitness gain with medium confidence. Prototype evidence is not an
accepted tournament result. The principal risks are formal correctness
in FIFO/replay invalidation corners and implementation drift that
restores tag-before-comparison selection or fetch/hazard feedback.
Verify actual RAM mapping, all unchanged formal/cosim gates,
canonical CoreMark CRCs and validation literal with both standard bus
stalls, marker-only cycles, OOB checks and all-option Gowin median.

title: Separate register-writer permission from branch-only trap decisions
motivation:
The champion reaches 223.44 iterations/second at 93.708 MHz with
4,193,876 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported 16.058 ns worst
vendor path starts at MEM/WB.write_value[14], passes through EX,
and ends at ID/EX.fwd_rs2_sel through the forwarding unit. The
current near-producer permission uses ctrl_with_trap.reg_write,
whose cancellation depends on misalign_branch as well as
misalign_jump. Branch misalignment depends on a full-width source
comparison even though every decoded branch already has reg_write=0.
Pipeline control registers obscure that implication from synthesis.
Prior complete bypass preselection and ALU-input preselection helped;
match-only retiming and extra shift pipeline stages did not remove
this remaining permission dependency. No prior micro_opt attempt
has explicitly separated branch-only traps from writer cancellation.

title: Cache successor comparison signatures alongside predicted targets
motivation:
Prediction recovery remains a timing limit after the champion's operand
and shifter improvements. The r9s2 worst path ran from MEM/WB forwarded
data to EX redirect through 31 cells, and r9s1 also exposed forwarding
to recovery timing. A canonical CoreMark ISS profile found only 1,194
ideal changing-return-target errors, insufficient headroom for a return
stack alone. Scratch prototypes moving target/inverse calculations
directly into ID preserved 4,193,876 CoreMark cycles and canonical CRCs,
but reduced median Gowin Fmax to 78.978 MHz, or 67.343 MHz with RAM16
banking. Their critical path became BTB lookup followed by inverse
arithmetic into ID/EX. This identifies the better predictor angle:
cache comparison operands during resolved training, so neither EX
forwarding nor the current fetch lookup feeds a serial carry chain
before prediction validation.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Augment the existing tagged 64-entry next-PC predictor with successor
comparison signatures. Preserve its two-bit direction policy, capacity,
fall-through skid, pipeline depth and EX/MEM-owned registered recovery.
A predicted target and its signature form one immutable accepted-fetch
token. Decode prepares only equality/validity bits from cached metadata;
it must not subtract the live predicted PC or compute a full static
target followed by equality on the fetch-to-ID/EX path.

For each allocated entry store its control kind (PC-relative branch/JAL
or JALR), whether its target equals that entry PC+4, and the PC-relative
displacement for branch/JAL entries. JALR entries additionally store
their signed 12-bit immediate and two full-width inverse rs1 candidates.
Extend resolved feedback with control kind, decoded displacement,
JALR immediate and the actual forwarded rs1. Generate signatures only
from this existing registered once-per-advance feedback. For a JALR
let s = resolved_rs1[0] XOR immediate[0]. Its two candidates are
resolved_rs1 - s and resolved_rs1 + (1-s), modulo 2^32. These equal
resolved_target - immediate and resolved_target + 1 - immediate because
JALR clears the sum's bit zero. The training lane therefore needs only
conditional increment/decrement, never a forwarding-to-wide-subtract
bypass into prediction. Calculate target-equals-PC+4 from registered
feedback. Write target, kind and signature together on allocation.

On a predicted-taken tagged hit capture the exact selected entry's
signature with predicted_next_pc. On miss or predicted-not-taken capture
a sequential signature: displacement 4, sequential-match true and no
usable JALR inverse signature. The skid retains every metadata field
with its instruction and PC. In ID compute static-target mismatch as
cached displacement != decoded immediate when the signature describes
a PC-relative successor; a JALR-kind signature conservatively mismatches
a static target. Sequential mismatch is the negation of the captured
exact target-equals-PC+4 flag. Register these narrow decisions in ID/EX,
together with the cached inverse candidates and a JALR-signature-usable
bit requiring a predicted JALR kind and an exact immediate match.

EX selects registered sequential/static mismatch with the resolved
outcome. For a usable JALR signature, compare the actual forwarded rs1
against both cached candidates in parallel. A match requires either
equality and predicted_next_pc[0]==0. This is exact for the captured
target, including odd bases, negative offsets and 32-bit wraparound.
If the signature kind or immediate does not match, or a sequential
prediction has no inverse signature, conservatively request recovery
to the actual architectural target even if the predicted PC happens
to equal it. This extra flush is safe and must be documented; never
accept an unverifiable prediction or reintroduce the full sum-to-PC
comparator as a fallback. Such cases primarily accompany BTB misses
or changed instructions. Keep actual JALR rs1+imm and branch/JAL PC+imm
adders in EX for architectural pc_next and redirect_target, in parallel
with these comparisons. No target arithmetic is moved into ID.

Physically bank all BTB payload into four constant-index RAM16 banks:
bank PC[7:6], word PC[5:2], full tag PC[31:8]. Resolve each bank's tag,
validity and direction locally before masked-OR target and signature
selection. Use asynchronous reads, synchronous bank-local writes and
distributed_ram attributes, resetting validity only. Keep independent
update-hit reads as needed for RAM inference. This supports the wider
signature table without BSRAM output-to-decode arithmetic; it is part
of this single predictor organization, with no replay or fetch FIFO.
Verify actual Gowin RAM16 mapping. Lookup observes the pre-edge entry
on simultaneous training, with no same-cycle feedback bypass.

Preserve exact tag validation and stale-entry invalidation for ordinary,
illegal and misaligned resolutions. A changed JALR immediate invalidates
usability of old inverse candidates even if the BTB tag still matches.
Hold all captured fields under original ID/EX and skid enables. Keep
alignment traps, untaken-misaligned-branch behavior, jump link writes,
one-shot training, retained older recovery through dmem stalls, younger
store/M-request squash, arithmetic and nret=1 RVFI order unchanged.
Never assume predicted control kind establishes decoder legality.

The final cached-signature architecture has not been synthesized; the
failed direct-calculation prototypes establish its timing constraints,
not an improvement claim. Expect about eight percent fitness gain from
removing prediction-check carry chains while retaining normal latency.
With unchanged 4,193,876 bracketed cycles, median Fmax must exceed

median across all Gowin placement options. No contract changes.

title: Retiming prediction validation behind registered execute resolution lanes
motivation:
The champion takes 4,193,876 bracketed CoreMark cycles at 93.708 MHz
and scores 223.44 iterations/second. Its reported critical path runs
from registered WB data through execute into decode bypass selection.

r9s1 ends at the redirect register through 40 cells, while r10s0 ends
at redirect_target through 41 cells. Splitting the shifter did not
remove these paths. The r10s1 attempt moved successor comparisons to
decode and instead made BTB lookup followed by equality critical.

cut: register independent resolution operands before comparing and
selecting the recovery successor, without another pipeline cycle.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace EX's registered final redirect decision and selected target
with a registered control-resolution payload owned by the same
EX/MEM token. In parallel during EX, capture sequential PC, the raw
control target, predicted next PC, branch condition, validated control
kind and target-alignment information. The raw control target chooses
JALR rs1+imm with bit zero cleared or the PC-relative branch/JAL target;
its capture must not depend on branch outcome, prediction mismatch or
recovery. No prediction arithmetic or comparison moves into ID.

From these registered fields, a small recovery module compares the
captured prediction against sequential and control successors in
parallel, selects the appropriate one-bit mismatch, and selects the
registered successor for redirect_target. Determine resolved taken
only from registered legality, alignment, kind and branch condition.
Its redirect is combinational from the EX/MEM owner; do not register
it again. Thus recovery reaches fetch and squashes the younger EX
token on the same edge as today's registered redirect. This removes
carry-chain-to-equality and outcome-to-wide-target-register paths
from EX without increasing ordinary latency or misprediction bubbles.

Hold resolution validity and payload exactly when EX/MEM is held by
dmem backpressure. Recovery remains asserted for its pending older
owner until that owner advances. Reset clears ownership. EX-wait
drains older tokens once and inserts invalid resolution tokens;
a redirect squashes the younger EX token and cancels its prospective
memory effect and MUL/DIV request. Carry predicted_next_pc coherently
with every normal and blocking-M completion token. Noncontrol and
illegal instructions must still recover stale taken predictions to

feedback, including branch target training for not-taken branches.

writes are suppressed on misalignment. Decode-side near-writer
permission must use validated reg_write and a dedicated two-bit

or the conditional-branch predicate back into bypass selection.

This writer qualification is part of the control-resolution boundary,
not a change to the decoder's legality policy or source priority.

title: Verify next-PC predictions from the registered EX/MEM successor
motivation:
The champion takes 4,193,876 bracketed CoreMark cycles at 93.708 MHz,
for fitness 223.44. Recent predictor-related timing limits include

its formal time budget. A simpler register boundary already exists:
EX/MEM carries the resolved architectural pc_next. Using that boundary
for exact prediction validation can split arithmetic from equality
without enlarging the BTB or adding a recovery cycle.

(out.pc_next != out.predicted_next_pc). Drive redirect_target from

and registered redirect state; never add a second recovery register.

same edge, so comparing their replacement registered operands during
the following interval preserves the existing recovery edge. The
critical path is split into forwarded resolution to successor capture
and registered equality to frontend recovery, rather than forwarding

escape. Preserve saved forwarded M operands and prediction metadata

motivation:

branch-only writer cancellation in r10s0 also exposed recovery as

permission across the existing producer register boundaries, while
