CoreMark cycles. Recent timing reports expose forwarding through target
addition and successor equality into registered recovery. Moving that
equality into decode or behind EX/MEM lost clock speed without saving
cycles. The r10s2 inverse-signature predictor instead failed the formal
time budget; it carried two JALR inverse operands and used a wider
banked lookup. Reuse its arithmetic-independent verification principle
with substantially less metadata and conservative exact-operand matching.

Fresh isolated probes on this champion also rejected RAM banking alone:
a four-bank 64-entry predictor measured 90.406 MHz median, while smaller
banked tables and shared-sector tags did not beat the champion. Preserve
the champion's existing table organization and recovery register.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Augment the existing 64-entry tagged next-PC predictor with one compact
certificate per entry. Each certificate has a 32-bit value, 12-bit
JALR immediate, JALR-kind bit and target-equals-PC+4 bit: 46 stored bits.
For a branch or JAL, value is its decoded sign-extended displacement;
for JALR, value is its actual forwarded rs1 operand. Record these fields
from the same registered once-per-advance EX feedback that supplies the
target. Derive target-equals-PC+4 from that registered PC and target.
Target, tag, control kind and certificate must be written coherently.

On an accepted predicted-taken tagged hit, capture the selected
certificate with the exact predicted_next_pc and a taken bit. On a
sequential prediction capture taken=0 and sequential-match=1. Preserve
this metadata through the fall-through skid and ID/EX under their
existing acceptance, hold, flush and recovery rules. ID only registers
the certificate; perform no certificate comparison or target arithmetic
on the fetch-to-decode path. Keep the original table size, full tags,
direction counters, pre-edge lookup and registered final recovery.
Do not add a lookup stage or the RAM banking that failed the probes.

In EX, independently compute architectural branch conditions, targets,
alignment faults, pc_next and redirect_target exactly as today. Replace
sum-to-predicted-PC equality with certificate validation. If the actual
successor is sequential, mismatch is captured_taken AND NOT captured
target-equals-PC+4. For a taken PC-relative branch/JAL, accept only a
captured taken prediction of PC-relative kind whose cached displacement
exactly equals the instruction's decoded immediate. Since the lookup
validated the complete instruction PC tag and training wrote target
and displacement together, this establishes the exact target without
a target-adder-to-equality chain.

For a legal aligned taken JALR, accept only captured_taken, cached JALR
kind, exact twelve-bit immediate equality, and exact full-width equality
of the forwarded rs1 with the cached operand. These comparisons run in
parallel with the existing rs1+imm adder. Otherwise conservatively
recover to the actual target, even if another operand would happen to
produce the same target after bit-zero clearing. One cached operand is
sufficient for correctness; the two inverse candidates and increment/
decrement training arithmetic from r10s2 are unnecessary. Do not add a
full target-equality fallback, which would restore the critical path.

Conservative recovery can add bubbles on cold predictions, changed
control encodings or equivalent odd/even JALR bases; measure these
costs instead of assuming exact cycle equivalence. Ordinary and illegal
instructions, alignment traps and completed M instructions still repair
stale taken predictions to PC+4. Invalid tokens never recover. A taken
misaligned control instruction traps and cancels jump link writes; an
untaken branch with a misaligned target keeps its current behavior.
Predictor kind never substitutes for the decoder's legality checks.

Keep once-only training and EX/MEM-owned recovery across dmem holds,
exact captured predictions, younger store/M-request squash, forwarded
operands, arithmetic/ALTOPS, bus handshakes and nret=1 RVFI order and
progress unchanged. Keep matching-only stale-entry invalidation and all
current correctness assertions. Measure canonical stalled CoreMark CRCs,
validation literal, bounds and marker cycles, and all vendor placement
options. Run every formal/cosim gate without weakening checks.

Expect seven percent fitness improvement through shorter prediction
verification, with low confidence until measured. At the champion's
cycle count, acceptance needs median Fmax above approximately 98.02 MHz;
use the actual cycle count if conservative recovery adds bubbles. Main
risks are wider certificate lookup routing, the separate forwarding/
alignment permission path, and formal solver cost from metadata-target
coherence. The compact certificate uses about half the additional
payload of the failed inverse-signature design and avoids its arithmetic.

title: Replicate registered bypass buses for local execute consumers
motivation:
The champion scores 223.44 at 93.708 MHz over 4,193,876 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. A fresh unchanged placement-option-0 build reproduces
92.907 MHz and its 16.058 ns worst path from MEM/WB.write_value[14]
through raw rs1 forwarding, branch/trap qualification and next-instruction
forwarding selection. That launch bit has fanout 10; its first route
alone costs 1.855 ns, followed by another 1.599 ns route into comparison.
Another near-critical ordinary-result path has ALU B bit-zero fanout 98.
The same producer words serve both complete ALU-input muxes and the raw
operand networks used by branches, JALR, addresses and stores.

LESSONS.md and the micro_opt history show that moving branch comparison,
writer permission or prediction verification has repeatedly exposed
another critical path. Local probes in this proposal worktree also
rejected carry-select target addition, shift-control preselection,
reordered shifts, result-capture factoring and operation predecode in
placement option 0. None established a gain. Their changes are excluded
from this hypothesis. Preserve the successful arithmetic and decision
networks and reduce the physical load on their common launch buses.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one physically distinct registered copy of each existing 32-bit
near and far bypass word, at the same EX/MEM and MEM/WB clock boundaries.
Partition consumers: retain the original producer buses for complete
alu_a_sel/alu_b_sel operand muxes and blocking arithmetic capture; use
the copies for the raw rs1/rs2 muxes feeding branch comparison, JALR,
effective addresses, stores and RVFI source values. Both source networks
keep the existing registered one-hot forwarding selections and newest
writer priority. There is no new bypass decision or pipeline stage.

The near copy captures exactly the same next result as EX/MEM.alu_result:
fast integer/link result, saved MUL completion, saved DIV completion or
zero bubble, under the existing reset, dmem hold, redirect, completion
and ex_wait priorities. The far copy captures exactly the same unified
value as MEM/WB.write_value, including the load/ALU selection, and must
retain its payload on hold_wb even when retirement valid is cleared.
Reset initializes both copies consistently with the original words.
Never obtain a copy by sampling the original Q on the next clock edge;
both flops must sample the same D on the original capture edge.

Declare each copy as a separate local register with Gowin-supported
syn_preserve/syn_keep attributes as appropriate. Confirm in the mapped
vendor netlist that both 32-bit copies survive register merging and
have separate consumer nets. A wire alias or a duplicate RTL assignment
optimized back into one flop is not this experiment. Replicate storage,
not the multiplier, divider, arithmetic operators or control logic.
Share each established next-result expression between the original and
its copy so replication adds register load without duplicating arithmetic.

Add internal execute/memory output ports and top-level wiring for the
replicated words. The core's external IO and nret=1 RVFI ports remain
exact. Arithmetic operands, forwarded source bits, alignment traps,
producer permissions, predictor contents/training, registered recovery,
load-use bubbles and all request/completion timing remain unchanged.
In particular, held consumers must see the retained far copy during
dmem stalls, and M completion must update the original and near copy
together before a dependent instruction advances. Preserve wrong-path
store/M squash, once-only memory effects and contiguous retirement.

This is a local fanout and routing micro-optimization, not a prediction
policy or pipeline topology change. It adds 64 payload flops while
retaining identical valid-cycle behavior and CoreMark cycles. Smaller
producer fanout should let Gowin place raw-operand launch flops closer
to branch/address logic and keep ALU launch flops nearer integer logic.
The benefit is a hypothesis, not a measured timing result. A predictor
path may take over, and added clock/D-input load may erase the gain.

Predict six percent fitness improvement with low confidence. Acceptance
requires actual fitness above 233.71824; at 4,193,876 cycles this means
median vendor Fmax above approximately 98.02 MHz. Check copy/original
equality over reset, valid tokens, bubbles, holds and M completions;
run unchanged formal/cosim and canonical stalled CoreMark CRC, UART,
bounds and marker checks. Measure all scored placement options and
reject replication that disappears in synthesis or fails to improve
the measured median. Do not weaken any existing correctness check.

title: Pipeline control resolution with registered MEM recovery and younger annul
motivation:
The champion achieves 223.44 iterations/second at 93.708 MHz over
4,193,876 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path runs from
MEM/WB.write_value through execute to ID/EX forwarding selection.
Separating writer permission alone in r10s0 exposed forwarded operands
through control-target generation to redirect_target as the next limit.
r11s1 moved prediction validation after EX/MEM but left its result
combinational through fetch-PC recovery, reducing Fmax to 83.346 MHz.
r12s1 removed live producer permission but introduced an extra choice
selection before EX's data masks, reducing Fmax to 85.146 MHz.
These outcomes suggest cutting the control lane with a second real
register boundary while retaining today's complete operand selections.

4,193,876 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path runs from

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Pipeline only control resolution across the existing EX/MEM and MEM/WB
boundaries. EX registers independent prediction, sequential successor,
raw control target, branch outcome, control kind and alignment evidence
alongside the instruction. A MEM-owned verification lane compares the
registered successors against the captured prediction and registers
both the final redirect and selected recovery target on the same edge
that the owner advances to MEM/WB. Fetch observes only that final
registered event and target. Ordinary ALU, memory and M-operation
result latency and the single-retirement pipeline remain unchanged.

This deliberately adds one cycle of misprediction recovery. Unlike
r11s1, no successor equality or target selection is combinational
between the recovery register and the fetch-PC register. Unlike r12s1,
EX retains its existing complete one-hot source and ALU selections;
do not add producer acceptance alternatives before its operand masks.

The recovery owner is now the instruction advancing to MEM/WB, so one
younger instruction may occupy EX/MEM when the event becomes visible.
Annul that younger MEM token before any memory handshake or retirement:
gate read/write enables with the registered recovery, insert an invalid
MEM/WB token instead of accepting it, squash the younger EX result and
flush ID and fetch skid. Preserve the older owner's MEM/WB retirement
and WB write; do not suppress it with the younger-token annul signal.
A killed younger memory instruction must not assert dmem backpressure
or prevent recovery from clearing. Generate recovery only when its
owner really advances, and retain verification payload with EX/MEM
through an older owner's dmem stall. This includes stale predictions
on ordinary instructions, stores, illegal instructions and completed
M operations: the owner executes once before younger effects are killed.
Invalidate each recovery event after its single consumption, including
consecutive redirects; reset cancels all pending ownership.

The intervening younger EX token may start a blocking MUL/DIV before
recovery is visible. Add an explicit synchronous cancellation input to
the existing M units and clear EX's M ownership and saved token on late
recovery. Any active M owner at that point is younger: an older blocking
M operation must complete before the recovering instruction can advance
through this in-order machine. Recovery suppresses same-cycle requests,
result acceptance and forwarding, overrides ex_wait in ID flush control,
and cancels the arithmetic FSMs without altering their real or ALTOPS
calculations. A canceled result must never reappear or retire; the next
correct-path M operation must start normally. No live MEM prediction
comparison is added to the M request or fetch control path.

Resolve full branch/jump alignment and RVFI pc_next/trap metadata from
the registered owner in MEM. Remove conditional-branch fault logic from
near-writer permission: branches cannot write a register. Near writer
qualification for jumps must still cancel a misaligned JAL/JALR before
a dependent instruction selects it. Compute that jump-only decision
using target low bits, including the two-bit forwarded rs1 + immediate
carry and JALR bit-zero clearing, without full-width successor equality
or branch comparison in decode's forwarding-permission cone. Preserve
youngest accepted writer priority, canceled-writer fallback, x0 and
the retained far WB value during stalls. MEM applies final control
traps before RF writeback and carries exact resolved PC and source
metadata into RVFI. Train the predictor once per accepted owner using
registered resolution, with no training bypass into fetch lookup.

Keep real and ALTOPS M arithmetic and capture uncanceled M operands once,
conservative load-use interlocks, stable waiting memory requests and
once-only effects. Preserve nret=1 and every top-level port, contiguous
channel-0 retirement, decoder legality, all existing formal/unit/cosim
checks, address bounds, canonical CRCs, UART validation and marker-only
timing. Add no assumption that instructions or memory are immutable.

Estimate a ten-percent net fitness gain, with medium confidence. The
prior extra recovery cycle in r7s1 increased CoreMark cycles by about
1.54 percent; a similar increment here would require over 99.53 MHz
median Gowin Fmax to clear the 4.6-percent acceptance threshold.
Use actual marker cycles, since stall phasing may change. The principal
risks are ALU or predictor paths becoming limiting, extra recovery
cycles exceeding the estimate, and new annul fanout offsetting the
registered control cut. The hypothesis is successful only if measured
fitness exceeds 233.71824 iterations/second with all correctness gates.

title: Validate predicted successors with parallel carry consistency
motivation:
The champion scores 223.44 at 93.708 MHz over 4,193,876 marker-bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Prior predictor experiments expose forwarded operands
through target addition and successor equality into registered recovery.
Moving equality into decode or after EX/MEM reduced Fmax; cached operand
certificates twice exceeded the formal timeout. Preserve the current
prediction table, metadata and recovery boundaries and replace the
arithmetic-dependent verification itself with an exact local relation.

Fresh scratch probes of eight-, twelve- and sixteen-bit folded BTB tags
measured median Gowin Fmax of 91.173, 78.279 and 93.681 MHz respectively.
They do not beat the champion and are not part of this proposal. Exact
carry-consistency verification avoids both wider predictor storage and
the correspondence proof needed for cached target certificates.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace EX's addition-then-equality successor checks with a parallel
carry-consistency verifier. For 32-bit operands A and B and captured
predicted sum P, infer each incoming carry as C = A XOR B XOR P.
Derive the outgoing carry independently at each bit as
G = (A AND B) OR ((A XOR B) AND NOT P).
The prediction is exactly A+B modulo 2^32 if and only if
C XOR {G[30:0], 1'b0} is zero. Bit zero checks the required initial
carry of zero; every higher bit checks one adjacent carry relation.
Do not check carry out of bit 31, since RV32 address addition wraps.
Compute all local relations in parallel followed by a balanced OR
reduction, instead of passing a completed carry-propagated sum into
a wide equality comparator. Use a helper function or explicit wires
compatible with both Gowin and the existing Yosys formal frontend.

Use this exact check with A=in.pc and B=4 for the sequential successor,
and A=in.pc and B=in.imm for PC-relative branch/JAL targets. For JALR
use A=the actual forwarded rs1 and B=in.imm, accounting exactly for
architectural clearing of the sum's bit zero. Set mismatch bit zero
to P[0], independently compute the true carry into bit one as
A[0] AND B[0], and compare it with inferred C[1]. Bits 2 through 31
use the same adjacent local relations as above. Merely masking the
ordinary verifier's bit zero is incorrect: it would infer the wrong
carry into bit one when the unclipped sum is odd. No cached operand,
inverse signature, predicted control type, shortened address, or
conservative extra recovery is needed.

Keep the existing actual target adders, forwarded branch comparison,
target-alignment traps, jump link value, resolved_taken selection,
computed_redirect_target, and architectural RVFI pc_next. Replace
only mismatch_sequential and mismatch_target. Select the JALR check
using the decoded is_jalr control, and select the final mismatch using
the actual resolved_taken exactly as today. Verification continues
for every valid advancing instruction, including ordinary instructions,
illegal instructions, alignment faults and completed M operations
carrying stale predictions. Invalid tokens never redirect. The exact
Boolean relation must produce precisely the old mismatch result for
every operand and captured prediction, preserving CoreMark cycles.

Preserve the original 64-entry full-tag BTB, direction counters,
registered once-per-advance predictor feedback, accepted-fetch and
fall-through skid behavior, all prediction metadata and stage widths.
Keep registered final recovery owned by EX/MEM and its target stable
through dmem stalls; recovery overrides bus readiness and queue fullness
and squashes every younger store and M request. Preserve decoder
validation, alignment gating, M arithmetic/ALTOPS, full bus handshakes,
nret=1 IO, exact RVFI retirement order and forward progress. Change no
evaluation files or formal assumptions.

Prove the helper equivalent to full 32-bit modular addition equality
for both ordinary and bit-zero-cleared modes using a standalone
combinational SAT miter. Exercise long carry chains, alternating bits,
negative offsets, overflow, all-zero/all-one words, arbitrary predicted
bits, odd/even equivalent JALR bases and mismatches at every bit. Retain
all existing EX and pipeline assertions. Require the unchanged full
formal/cosim gates, canonical stalled CoreMark CRCs and validation
literal, marker-only cycles, bounds and median Gowin timing.

Expect six percent fitness improvement, with low confidence pending
measurement. At unchanged 4,193,876 cycles, acceptance needs median
Fmax above approximately 98.02 MHz. The potential gain comes solely
from shorter exact prediction verification with no additional recovery
or fetch latency. Risks are local-check reduction routing, duplication
of verification logic alongside actual target adders, and the existing
forwarding-permission path remaining dominant. Prototype measurements,
if recorded here, do not constitute a full formal or tournament pass.

title: Co-capture low-word MUL completion at the EX/MEM boundary
motivation:
The champion scores 223.44 at 93.708 MHz over 4,193,876 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md shows that capturing forwarded multiply
operands before DSP arithmetic was a successful timing cut in r3s1.
Recent comparison, forwarding and recovery experiments have failed
to clear the acceptance threshold. The current low-word MUL captures
operands, computes a registered product, then transfers that product
into EX/MEM on another edge. That last transfer is a candidate for a
redundant cycle: the already registered operands can instead feed
product computation directly into the existing EX/MEM result register.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Optimize only the low-word MUL completion schedule. Keep its initial
request edge capturing forwarded operands and operation exactly as
today. During the following MUL_CALC cycle, compute the unsigned
product from mul_a_q and mul_b_q, never from live forwarding operands.
Expose its low 32 bits as an early completion and assert result_valid
for MUL_CALC when the captured operation is ALU_MUL. The existing
owned-completion branch in ex_stage then captures this result and
the saved instruction into EX/MEM on the product-calculation edge.
EX releases the held ID/EX token on this same acceptance edge. This
removes one MUL completion-transfer cycle without removing the operand
register boundary, adding a bypass source, or changing pipeline topology.

Define one shared combinational product_next expression from the
captured operands. Continue capturing that expression into the existing
product register in MUL_CALC. If the early low-word completion is
accepted, transition directly to MUL_IDLE. If downstream dmem stalls
prevent acceptance, transition to MUL_DONE with the product registered;
subsequent completion cycles use its registered low half. The early
and retained results must be bit-identical across this transition, and
result_valid must stay asserted until acceptance. This preserves stable
held completion data without recomputing from changing external inputs.

Keep MULH/MULHU/MULHSU on their current CALC, HIGH, DONE path, including
the unsigned 64-bit product and signed high-half correction. Preserve
divider arithmetic and all DIV/REM timing. Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS,
compute the existing exact abstraction from captured operands and
operation through product_next; low-word MUL uses the same early/held
completion schedule, while high operations retain their correction
stage and established abstraction results. Do not change any formula.

Preserve existing request-ready arbitration, mutual M ownership,
reset cancellation, saved source/retirement metadata, and consumer
forwarding. An early completion cannot occur on the initial operand
capture cycle. Older dmem backpressure continues to hold EX/MEM and
ID/EX; a stalled MUL completion cannot overwrite an older memory token.
On acceptance the result must enter EX/MEM exactly once, and a dependent
consumer's existing near-selection must refer to that captured result.
A request offered while busy is accepted only on an actual ready edge.
Keep pending recovery, wrong-path M/store suppression, load-use bubbles,
retained WB data, predictor policy/training and every instruction other
than low-word MUL at their established cycle behavior.

Preserve nret=1 and all external ports, decoder legality/defaults,
exact RVFI operands/results/PC/traps, contiguous retirement, address
bounds, stable memory handshakes, once-only effects and forward progress.
Keep all existing assertions; update the low-word MUL latency expectation
to the intentionally earlier completion instead of deleting checks.
Require unchanged formal/cosim gates and canonical stalled CoreMark
CRCs, UART validation, memory bounds and start/stop-marker timing.

The proposed gain comes from reducing blocking matrix-multiply cycles
while preserving the timing cut between forwarding and multiplication.
Confidence is low pending measured score. Product-to-EX/MEM completion
selection and DSP output-register inference may lower Fmax; the actual
cycle reduction must outweigh that loss. Acceptance requires measured
fitness above 233.71824, using median Gowin Fmax and actual marker cycles.
A scratch implementation and vendor measurement are being used to test
this mechanism; full correctness and acceptance remain implementation
gates. No evaluation files or correctness contract changes are proposed.

title: Elastic operand capture separates bypass and load completion from execute
motivation:
The champion scores 223.44 iterations/second at 93.708 MHz over
4,193,876 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path runs from
MEM/WB.write_value through EX control/trap qualification to the next
ID/EX forwarding selection. Recent structural attempts moved this
problem without removing the operand-to-execution chain: r12s1 added
forwarding alternatives before the ALU and lost 9.14 percent; r13s1
registered MEM recovery but gained only 1.42 percent after its extra
recovery cycle. A register boundary after actual operand selection
would isolate arithmetic and branch logic from those input muxes.

The earlier r4s1 operand-stage proposal was broken by stalled random3
cosim, with no FPGA result, rather than demonstrating a timing loss.
Revisit that structural split with explicit persistent operand ownership
and replay-safe stage handshakes. Retain the champion's distributed-RAM
register file, grouped shifter, predictor and registered M arithmetic.

A fresh reference trace of the unchanged canonical 2K, -O3 CoreMark ELF
between its MMIO markers contains 2,922,015 instructions, 544,852 loads,
203,959 immediate load consumers and 156,914 load consumers with one
intervening instruction. Waiting for registered WB data at the new
operand boundary would expose about 360,873 extra bubble candidates,
already 8.60 percent of champion cycles before recovery costs. Unlike
r4s1, capture accepted MEM load completions into the new operand register
to preserve existing load-use latency. These are architectural trace
counts, not measured cycles for the proposed machine.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Insert one registered operand-collection boundary between the decoded
ID/EX token and execute. Decode holds a D/O token; the new O/X register
contains fully resolved raw rs1/rs2, preselected ALU a/b, PC+4,
PC-relative target, prediction, validated controls and RVFI metadata.
Integer ALU, branch comparison, effective-address and JALR calculation
read only O/X registers. Remove live EX/MEM and MEM/WB operand muxes
from their input paths. This is one pipeline-topology change, with no
additional fetch stage, cache, prediction policy or retirement channel.

Preserve one instruction per cycle for adjacent ordinary ALU producers
and consumers using a same-cycle executing-X-result-to-O/X-register
bypass. Its endpoint is the next operand register, never a current X
input. Source priority is the youngest matching older instruction in
X, then EX/MEM, then MEM/WB, then the architectural RF snapshot.
EX/MEM supplies a registered ALU value or the current accepted load
completion, selected by its registered instruction kind. Distinguish
a matching producer's ownership from its result readiness;
a pending youngest load or M instruction blocks that source rather
than exposing an older same-rd value. Never bypass a load address.
Only actual legal source uses create execution interlocks. Preserve
architecturally correct RVFI raw operands for every source field the
existing contract reports. For fields unused by the legal datapath,
reconstruct the prewrite architectural value at retirement using an
RVFI-only shadow register file updated exactly once per valid retirement.
This preserves the reference's raw instruction-field convention without
stalling an ADDI on a register number encoded in its immediate. Used
sources must still report the actual captured execution values, so RVFI
continues to detect incorrect forwarding. The shadow has deterministic
reset/x0 behavior and no fanout into timed execution or bus controls.

Make operand ownership persistent across holds. Each D/O source keeps
either a resolved value or the identity of its youngest older pending
producer. Snoop the correct accepted producer result or WB write into
a held token before that producer disappears. Once resolved, retain
the value until the consumer transfers or is squashed; do not allow an
older retained WB slot, cleared retirement-valid bit, or reused stage
position to overwrite it. Producer identity must follow the instruction
through stage movement, not an unversioned physical slot. Capture both
sources independently and preserve same-rd writer age. Reset and
recovery discard younger pending identities and values together.
Use a narrow instruction tag carried through X, EX/MEM and MEM/WB;
a three-bit sequence suffices with at most three older live producers
while D/O holds. Reuse only after prior ownership has drained or been
canceled. Do not introduce the 64-bit RVFI order counter into timed
source matching, a rename table, or an out-of-order issue mechanism.

Establish actual write permission before releasing a matching source:
x0, illegal instructions and alignment-trapped writers cannot provide
an architectural result. In particular, cancel a misaligned jump using
the low target bits from registered X operands; conditional branches
have no destination. Resolve EX/MEM load alignment before treating a
load as a live pending writer. A canceled producer leaves the preceding
architectural value available through the older matching writer or
retained RF/WB value; it must not poison dependency ownership.

Add a MEM-completion-to-O/X-register bypass. Reuse mem_stage's exact
byte/halfword extraction and sign extension, and qualify its data with
a valid legal aligned load, io_dmemReady, matching producer identity,
absence of recovery and an actual owner advance. The destination is
only the operand register; no combinational load data enters the current
X arithmetic, branch predicate or recovery computation. MEM/WB captures
the same result on that edge for ordinary WB and retirement. Predecode
producer matches and instruction kind where possible and use one flat
data selection into O/X, rather than nesting a second priority mux.
This sustains the existing one bubble for an immediate load consumer
and no new bubble with one intervening instruction. Unaccepted loads
retain ownership and cannot release a consumer during dmem stalls.
When O waits for an operand and X can drain, retain D/O and fetch and
inject an invalid O/X token. When X owns unfinished MUL/DIV, retain
O/X and younger tokens while older stages drain. On M completion,
transfer its result and metadata once, and permit the completion value
to satisfy a waiting O source. Real and ALTOPS arithmetic, captured M
operands, held completion and reset semantics remain exact.

Use explicit, separate consume/refill events at D/O, O/X and EX/MEM.
Older dmem backpressure preserves stable EX/MEM requests and freezes
stage transfers; WB can retire its already-valid token once and retain
its forwarding payload. Operand bookkeeping may capture an older WB
value during that freeze without changing instruction ownership.
Never infer a fresh producer or consumer transfer just because a held
stage is valid. Bubbles cannot issue memory, start M, write RF, redirect
or train, and no stage may retire or accept a store more than once.

Compute final prediction mismatch and recovery target in X from its
registered operands and prepared PC values, retaining today's registered
EX/MEM-owned redirect and predictor feedback. An older recovery annuls
every younger D/O and O/X token before any X request or memory effect,
has priority over operand waits, and preserves the recovery owner's
EX/MEM instruction through dmem holds. Flush the fetch skid as today.
Correct predictions stream at one instruction per cycle; an error has
one additional younger pipeline slot. Preserve full-width PC/address
arithmetic, all alignment traps, exact RVFI operands/PCs and strictly
contiguous single-channel retirement with the unchanged nret=1 ports.

Budget roughly two percent more marker cycles, 4,277,754, for additional
recovery latency and changed stall phasing; load dependency bubbles
should remain at their existing latency. This is an estimate, not
measured IPC. At that count, acceptance needs median Gowin Fmax above
about 99.98 MHz. A 108 MHz median would yield about 252.47 iterations/
second, a 12.99 percent gain. Predict twelve percent with medium
confidence. Main risks are the X-result or load-completion capture
bypass becoming critical, frontend limits, additional mispredictions
from later training and register/ownership placement cost. Use
measured marker cycles and vendor median Fmax; require fitness above
233.71824 and every existing formal, unit, random stalled cosim, CRC,
UART, address-bound and timing-bracket gate. Do not change eval files.

title: Verify predicted control targets with short parallel carry segments
motivation:
The champion scores 223.44 at 93.708 MHz over 4,193,876 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its prediction recovery includes forwarded JALR
operands through a 32-bit target adder and successor equality. Moving
verification into decode or behind EX/MEM reduced Fmax, and cached
operand certificates twice timed out in formal. The prior bitwise
carry-consistency verifier passed correctness but scored 220.65;
its fine-grained Boolean network did not improve median timing.

Fresh isolated predictor-storage probes also rejected expanding the
64-entry table into registers and reducing it to a compact associative
table. Preserve the proven predictor and instead test a different exact
verification mapping: several short FPGA carry segments in parallel,
with no full-word carry propagation feeding target equality.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only EX's mismatch_target calculation with an exact parallel
four-bit segmented verifier. Retain the ordinary sequential-PC equality,
full architectural target adders, branch comparisons and registered
final recovery. The verifier uses the captured predicted_next_pc itself
to infer segment input carries, then checks each short sum and the
consistency of adjacent segments. This is a predictor verification
change, with no prediction table or pipeline topology change.

For A, B and predicted sum P, infer the per-bit incoming carry vector
C = A XOR B XOR P. Split the words into eight four-bit segments. Segment
j computes a five-bit S_j = {0,A[4j+:4]} + {0,B[4j+:4]} + c_j, with
c_0=0 and c_j=C[4j] for j>0. A segment reports mismatch if its low four
sum bits differ from P[4j+:4]. For j<7 also report mismatch if its carry
out S_j[4] differs from C[4j+4]. OR all segment mismatches through a
balanced reduction. Ignore carry out of the highest segment, since
RV32 addition wraps modulo 2^32. Each segment is independent and has
at most a short four-bit carry chain; no segment's computed carry feeds
another segment's adder. Prefer explicit fixed generate blocks or an
unrolled compatible helper so Gowin can infer its short native carry
structures, rather than a 32-bit adder followed by equality.

For branch/JAL use A=in.pc, B=in.imm and P=in.predicted_next_pc.
For JALR use the actual forwarded rs1 and decoded immediate. Because
JALR clears sum bit zero, reconstruct an unchecked raw predicted sum
P_raw={predicted_next_pc[31:1], rs1[0] XOR imm[0]}. Run the same segmented
verifier on A=rs1, B=imm and P_raw, and independently mismatch when
predicted_next_pc[0] is one. This restores the true raw sum bit zero
and therefore the correct carry into bit one. Simply masking an
ordinary verification error at bit zero is incorrect. Keep exact full
32-bit equivalence for both modes, including negative offsets, odd
JALR bases and address wraparound. No conservative extra recovery is
allowed; the mismatch must exactly equal the existing comparison.

Keep actual branch/JAL/JALR target calculation, bit-zero clearing,
misalignment traps, jump link writes, resolved_taken selection,
computed_redirect_target and architectural RVFI pc_next unchanged.
Verification still applies to all valid advancing instructions through
the original outcome-select logic, including stale predictions on
ordinary, illegal, misaligned and completed M instructions. Invalid
bubbles must never redirect. Do not add certificate state, a decoded
predicted kind, a training dependency or an extra stage.

Preserve the original 64-entry full-tag predictor and counter policy,
pre-edge lookup, fall-through skid acceptance and captured prediction
metadata through holds. Retain once-only registered training and
EX/MEM-owned recovery with a stable target across dmem holds, priority
over queue fullness and imem readiness, and squash of every younger
store and M request. Preserve arithmetic/ALTOPS, all bus handshakes,
nret=1 IO, decoder validation, RVFI order and forward progress.

Prove the helper against ordinary modular sum equality and bit-zero-
cleared JALR sum equality with a standalone combinational SAT miter.
Retain existing tests and exercise every segment boundary, long carries,
overflow, negative offsets, all-zero/all-one operands, arbitrary
predicted-bit errors and odd/even equivalent JALR bases. Require all
unchanged formal/cosim gates and canonical stalled CoreMark CRCs,
validation literal, bounds, marker-only cycles and median Gowin timing.

Expect six percent fitness improvement with low confidence through
shorter predictor verification, at exactly unchanged CoreMark cycles.
Acceptance needs median Fmax above approximately 98.02 MHz. Unlike the
prior bitwise verifier, this proposal deliberately retains short local
arithmetic carries and leaves the sequential comparator untouched.
Risks are short-adder mapping, reduction routing, duplicated logic
beside the actual target adders and another execute path remaining
dominant. Scratch timing is evidence about mapping, not a formal or
tournament improvement claim.

title: Flatten execute successor comparison and recovery selection
motivation:
The champion scores 223.44 iterations/second at 93.708 MHz over
4,193,876 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Recent worst Gowin paths repeatedly
reach EX redirect or redirect_target from forwarded operands. Moving
recovery across stages, replacing branch comparison, duplicating bypass
buses and shortening multiply completion all missed acceptance.

EX currently selects a full-width JALR versus PC-relative control target,
compares that selected word to the prediction, and selects the recovery
address against PC+4. This leaves target-type steering after forwarded
arithmetic and before equality, plus serial wide recovery selection.
Retain native arithmetic and compare the candidate successors before
selection. Earlier carry-consistency verification tried changing the
arithmetic verifier; this proposal changes only selection ordering.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Flatten the combinational execute successor network at its existing
registered recovery boundary. This is one local micro-optimization of
mux placement, with no new state, pipeline stage, predictor policy,
instruction latency or recovery cycle.

Retain the native full-width PC+immediate target adder, forwarded
rs1+immediate JALR adder, architectural JALR bit-zero clearing,
PC+4, branch predicates and resolved_taken. Define the existing
target-type choice as T = in.ctrl.is_jump && in.ctrl.is_jalr.
Compute two independent mismatch bits:
  relative_mismatch = predicted_next_pc != branch_target;
  indirect_mismatch = predicted_next_pc != {jalr_sum[31:1],1'b0}.
Set mismatch_target = T ? indirect_mismatch : relative_mismatch.
Keep mismatch_sequential and the original resolved_taken mismatch
selection unchanged. Thus target-type selection acts on one bit
after equality instead of selecting thirty-two bits before equality.
Both comparisons use actual complete architectural sums. Do not use
signatures, carry certificates, truncated addresses or conservative
extra redirects.

Express computed_redirect_target as a flat parallel mask-and-OR of
three complete successors, using mutually exclusive lane predicates:
  sequential lane: !resolved_taken;
  PC-relative lane: resolved_taken && !T;
  indirect lane: resolved_taken && T.
Sequential selects sequential_pc, PC-relative selects branch_target,
and indirect selects the bit-zero-cleared jalr_sum. Do not feed the
already selected control_target through another wide mux. Keep
control_target and its existing consumers for training, alignment and
architectural retirement unchanged; the optimization is confined to
prediction mismatch and the registered recovery-address input.

The resulting mismatch and recovery target must be bit-identical to
the original expressions for every operand and control combination,
including non-control, illegal, misaligned and completed M tokens.
Preserve valid advancing qualification and invalid-token suppression.
Keep the EX/MEM recovery register, dmem hold enable, owner retention
and target stability, once-only predictor update, skid discard and
younger store/M squash exactly as established. Do not move any
comparison into decode or after EX/MEM. Leave all arithmetic including
shifts, multiplication/division and ALTOPS unchanged, together with
operand preselection, writer/trap permissions, load-use interlocks,
retained WB forwarding, full addresses, nret=1 ports and RVFI ordering.

Prove the original and flattened combinational expressions equivalent
for arbitrary full-width successors, predictions and control bits.
Preserve all existing tests and cover PC-relative/JALR type switching,
negative offsets, long carries, wraparound, forwarded indirect targets,
odd JALR bases, exact alignment traps and incorrect predicted bits.
Exercise prolonged dmem holds and full-skid recovery. Require all
unchanged formal/cosim gates and canonical stalled CoreMark CRCs,
validation UART literal, bounds and marker-only cycles.

Predict six percent fitness improvement with low confidence by removing
a wide selection before target equality and flattening the recovery
address input, at exactly unchanged CoreMark cycles. Acceptance requires
median Gowin Fmax above approximately 98.02 MHz and fitness above
233.71824. Duplicate equality routing, high-fanout lane predicates,
synthesis merging comparisons back behind selection, and an unrelated
ALU/forwarding path becoming dominant are the main risks. Inspect all

title: Register resolved operands before execute with accepted-load capture
motivation:
The champion scores 223.44 iterations/second at 93.708 MHz and
4,193,876 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its recorded worst path runs from
MEM/WB write_value through EX into decode forwarding selection.
The current pipeline registers forwarding choices, but still places
data selection before arithmetic, target alignment and producer
permission. Additional retiming of choices or recovery alone has not
crossed the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold: r12s1 lost 9.14 percent,
and r13s1 gained only 1.42 percent after its extra recovery cycle.

A physical register boundary after resolved operand selection remains
the strongest unmeasured structural opportunity. The r4s1 attempt
failed stalled random3 cosim; r14s1 failed the sandbox gate because
its implementation left local logs in forbidden paths. Neither has
a valid FPGA result for this topology. Revisit the split with explicit
once-only transfers and durable source values, retaining the current
predictor, distributed-RAM RF, grouped shifter and registered M units.
Capturing accepted MEM load data at the new boundary avoids the extra
load-use penalty of waiting another cycle for registered WB data.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Insert a registered operand-collection stage between the current
decoded ID/EX token and execute. The decoded token becomes D/O; a new
O/X token contains resolved raw rs1/rs2, selected ALU a/b, prepared
PC+4 and PC-relative target, prediction, validated controls and RVFI
metadata. Arithmetic, branch predicates, effective-address and JALR
addition must read O/X registers exclusively. Eliminate live EX/MEM
and MEM/WB input muxes from X. This is one pipeline-topology change;
keep fetch buffering, predictor policy and retirement width intact.

Retain one-instruction-per-cycle ALU dependency chains with a fast
X-result-to-O/X-register bypass. Its endpoint is the next operand
register, never a current X input, so there is no combinational loop.
Select the youngest actual older writer in X, EX/MEM, MEM/WB, then
the RF snapshot. Separate matching ownership from readiness: a
younger unfinished load or M writer blocks its source, rather than
falling through to an older same-rd result or forwarding an address.
Use flat, independently decoded register-input selections. Reuse the
current trap-qualified writer semantics, including x0, illegal
instructions and canceled misaligned jumps/loads. An instruction
that cannot architecturally write rd must not acquire that dependency.
Establish X load writer permission from its effective-address low bits
and decoded width before assigning pending ownership; MEM continues
to enforce and report the alignment trap. Likewise establish actual
JAL/JALR permission from target alignment in X. Exclude conditional
branch comparison from writer permission because branches never write
rd. A canceled writer selects the next older writer or RF value without
leaving an unresolved dependency on a result that will never exist.

Expose mem_stage's existing extended load value as an accepted
completion and capture it directly into O/X. Qualify this event with
valid legal aligned LOAD ownership, io_dmemReady and actual memory
advance. MEM/WB captures the identical value on the same edge. No
live memory data may enter current X arithmetic or branch resolution.
This preserves one bubble for an immediate load consumer and zero
new bubbles with one intervening instruction, on a zero-wait stream.
A stalled or trapped load cannot release a waiting source. Preserve
byte/halfword/word extraction, sign extension and all memory masks.

A held D/O consumer must keep each resolved source after its producer
leaves a forwarding stage. Capture accepted matching X, MEM or WB
results into durable per-source state even when the other source is
unavailable or downstream is held. Once a source is resolved, retain
that exact value until transfer, reset or squash. Identify unresolved
sources with a narrow instruction-generation tag carried through
X, EX/MEM and MEM/WB; do not use reusable unversioned slot numbers.
Three bits suffice for this bounded, single-issue in-order pipeline,
provided tags are allocated only on real token creation and are not
reused while any live instruction or pending source still refers to
them. Recovery discards younger references before reusing tags.
Never let a stale retained WB payload overwrite a newer same-rd
value. No rename table or out-of-order issue is needed.
Bind ownership before marking an RF snapshot resolved. This decision
must include every older producer present when a D/O token is accepted,
and producer movement on the same consume/refill edge; a disappearing
valid bit must not make a pending writer appear absent. Generation
matches release only their owner, and a saved resolved value has
priority over later irrelevant WB writes to the same register number.

Interlock only actual legal execution sources. The existing raw
instruction-field RVFI convention must still be preserved for unused
fields whose bits happen to encode a register number. If these values
are reconstructed at retirement, use an RVFI-only shadow RF updated
exactly once per valid architectural write, with reset/x0 behavior
matching the current RF. Used sources must report the actual O/X
values consumed by execution, never replacement shadow values.
The shadow must have no fanout into timed execution or bus controls.
This avoids introducing extra execution dependencies on immediate
bits without hiding any real operand-routing error from verification.

Use explicit consume/refill events at D/O, O/X and EX/MEM. When O
waits for a source, hold D/O and fetch and bubble O/X if X can drain.
When X owns unfinished MUL/DIV, hold O/X and younger tokens while
older work drains. M operands come from O/X registers; request,
result and saved metadata transfer exactly once. A completed M value
may also satisfy an O source on its acceptance edge. Keep real and
ALTOPS arithmetic, high-word correction and result backpressure exact.
Older dmem backpressure retains stable EX/MEM requests and freezes
instruction movement. WB retires its prior token once while its
forwarding payload remains available. Bookkeeping may capture that
WB value during a hold without transferring a consumer instruction.
Stage valid by itself must never imply a new acceptance or retirement.

Keep the current registered EX/MEM-owned recovery and predictor
feedback. Compute the final mismatch and recovery target in X from
O/X operands and prepared PC values; do not move wide comparisons
into fetch/decode or onto the registered recovery-to-PC path. Older
recovery cancels all younger D/O and O/X tokens before an M request,
memory effect or producer event, and takes precedence over operand
waits. Preserve the recovery owner's EX/MEM token and target through
dmem holds. Correct predictions still stream at one instruction per
cycle; errors incur one additional younger slot. Reset cancels every
new validity, source ownership and M state. Preserve full-width PC
and address arithmetic, alignment traps, exact RVFI metadata and
strictly contiguous retirement on the unchanged nret=1 interface.

Budget two percent more bracketed cycles, approximately 4,277,754,
for recovery latency and changed stall phasing. This is an estimate,
not measured IPC. At that count the acceptance threshold requires
median Gowin Fmax above approximately 99.98 MHz; 108 MHz would score
about 252.47 iterations/second, roughly a thirteen percent gain.
Predict twelve percent. The main risks are X-result or accepted-load
capture becoming critical, frontend timing, delayed predictor training,
and extra ownership/control routing. Require measured fitness above
233.71824 with all existing formal, stalled random cosim, arithmetic,
memory-bound, CRC, UART and marker-timing gates passing. Run stalled
random3 cosim early because it broke the earlier operand-stage attempt.
Build and evaluation logs must stay in an allowed temporary directory
or the existing ignored build directories; create no tracked local
logs, change no evaluation file and weaken no check.

title: Compact branch-discovered replay with bank-local fetch decisions
motivation:
The champion reaches 223.44 at 93.708 MHz over 4,193,876 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Prior predictor experiments show little remaining
benefit from more BTB entries or a return stack, while cached target
certificates timed out in formal and two exact successor-verification
changes failed to improve fitness. Instruction stream replay has larger
measured headroom under the contracted instruction-bus stalls: eight
sixteen-word banks saved 9.33 percent of cycles, but their frontend

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion reaches 223.44 at 93.708 MHz over 4,193,876 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Prior predictor experiments show little remaining
benefit from more BTB entries or a return stack, while cached target
certificates timed out in formal and two exact successor-verification
changes failed to improve fitness. Instruction stream replay has larger
measured headroom under the contracted instruction-bus stalls: eight
sixteen-word banks saved 9.33 percent of cycles, but their frontend
routing and registered queue reduced Fmax enough to miss acceptance.
Test a smaller replay directory with local hit/data decisions and the
champion's existing fall-through fetch boundary.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a compact branch-discovered instruction stream predictor containing
four directly indexed 64-byte replay blocks, totaling 64 instruction
words. Retain the existing 64-entry tagged next-PC predictor, its exact
counter policy, registered recovery and one-entry fall-through skid.
This is one instruction stream replay hypothesis; the smaller directory
and bank-local implementation seek to retain its instruction-stall
savings without the large replay frontend's clock penalty.

Each constant-index generated replay bank owns sixteen unreset 32-bit
distributed_ram words, sixteen fill-valid bits, a full PC[31:8] tag and
one block-valid bit. Fetch PC[7:6] selects a bank and PC[5:2] selects a
word. Independently read, compare full tags, check the selected word's
validity and qualify the bank index inside each bank. Mask each bank's
instruction word with that bank's hit and OR the four masked words;
reduce the local hits for replay availability. Do not multiplex full
tags or fill bitmaps before comparing them, and do not bank or enlarge
the original next-PC table as part of this hypothesis.

Discover blocks only from once-only registered feedback for legal,
aligned, taken conditional backward branches whose inclusive
target-to-branch interval is at most 128 bytes. Register a discovery
mask and candidate full tags before applying directory changes. Allocate
every aligned 64-byte block intersecting the interval. This spans at
most three blocks and cannot allocate two different tags to one bank
in a transaction. Handle crossing a 256-byte bank-index boundary using
full addresses. Matching rediscovery retains filled words; a tag
replacement clears that bank's fill bitmap. Keep blocks across ordinary
redirects and loop exits, and never repeatedly consume held feedback.

Observe real imemReady words at the current presented fetch address to
fill matching allocated banks, even if decode or the skid is held.
Payload write enables depend only on ready bus data and that bank's
full-tag ownership, never on decode hazards, fetch_accept or redirect.
Replay words never fill themselves. Replacement, reset and instruction
invalidation override word-valid setting, so an old-owner write on a
replacement edge cannot become valid for the new owner. Reset validity
only and verify that payload storage infers RAM16.

Prefer the current ready instruction bus word. When imemReady is low,
a matching filled replay word supplies a valid fetch token. Internal
source availability becomes imemReady OR replay_hit. Preserve the
existing empty-skid bypass, head priority, simultaneous drain/refill,
fetch acceptance and exact captured predicted_next_pc. No extra token
register or queue-refill cycle is added. Recovery overrides source
readiness and skid fullness and discards all younger tokens. EX still
resolves every architectural successor and validates forwarded operands
and target alignment; replay bypasses no hazard or execution checks.

Add a FENCE.I bit to predictor_update_t from a legal advancing opcode
0x0f/funct3=1 instruction. Force its registered recovery to PC+4 and
invalidate all replay ownership/fill validity, canceling every pending
discovery ahead of fills and allocation. Flush prefetched younger
instructions through the existing recovery path. Invalidation must
complete before any post-FENCE.I token can issue. Preserve decoder
legality and the existing architectural NOP result of FENCE/FENCE.I.

Preserve full address tags, one-shot BTB training, pre-edge lookup,
EX/MEM recovery ownership and stable targets across dmem holds,
younger store/M-request squash, all RV32M/ALTOPS arithmetic, bus
handshakes, nret=1 ports, retirement order and every existing assertion.
Change no evaluation or formal-contract file. Validate reset and
replacement concurrent with fills, bank-index wrap, upper-tag aliases,
changing code with FENCE.I, both bus stalls and bounded progress.

Expect six percent fitness gain with low confidence. This is an
unmeasured capacity/timing tradeoff: fewer retained loops can reduce
the previous replay cycle saving, while fall-through hit-to-hazard
routing can still constrain Fmax. At a six percent cycle reduction,
acceptance requires median Fmax above approximately 92.14 MHz; compute
the actual requirement from measured marker cycles rather than assuming
unchanged timing. Require all unchanged formal/cosim gates, canonical
CoreMark CRCs and validation literal, memory bounds, marker-only cycles,
and median Gowin timing across all placement options.
